extraction_notes.note: Remark environment retyped as theorem (external, standard): its content is a restatement of the parallelogram law; the closing sentence that Corollary 4 generalizes it is recorded as a generalizes edge.
Theorem or definition: the sentence both asserts that (5) holds in CAT(0) spaces and introduces the names CAT(0)/Hadamard/global NPC spaces; kept as an external theorem.

Lemma 13 restates Lemma 9 (ii) verbatim. Both are numbered environments, so Lemma 13 is kept as its own node (it has the proof) and linked to the claim for Lemma 9 (ii) by a uses edge instead of being merged via also_stated_at.
Proofs titled 'that X implies Y' were resolved by syntax to X; their proves edges were set to Y (Theorem 4 and Theorem 3) by hand.
Lemma 9 has no proof environment: its two parts are proved case by case in Sections B.3-B.9 by Lemmas 13-20, so the parts are claims nested in Lemma 9 and receive uses edges from those lemmas.

The description of the computer-assisted numerical search in Section 4, the tables, the tikz figures and the outline paragraphs were not extracted; the dependency-overview figure is absent from the source.
The opening paragraph of Appendix B (density argument and quotient convention) is kept as one remark; it is used implicitly by all appendix proofs but no edge is drawn.

nodes.name: Cauchy–Schwarz inequality
nodes.statement: \langle u,v \rangle \leq \normof{u} \normof{v}
conclusions: \label{eq:csi} \langle u,v \rangle \leq \normof{u} \normof{v}
nodes.label: eq:csi

nodes.name: Distance shorthand
nodes.statement: In any metric space $(\mc Q, d)$ the triangle inequality \begin{equation} \ol yz \leq \ol yp + \ol pz \end{equation} is true for all $p,y,z\in\mc Q$, where we use the short notation $\ol yz := d(y,z)$.

nodes.name: Triangle inequality
nodes.statement: \ol yz \leq \ol yp + \ol pz
conclusions: \label{eq:tri} \ol yz \leq \ol yp + \ol pz
nodes.label: eq:tri

nodes.name: Quadruple inequality with constant L_tau
nodes.statement: Consider the inequality \begin{equation} \tau(\ol yq) - \tau(\ol yp) - \tau(\ol zq) + \tau(\ol zp) \leq \ctrano{\tau}\, \ol qp \, \tau^\prime(\ol yz) \end{equation} for $y,z,q,p\in\mc Q$, a differentiable function $\tau\colon[0,\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$ with derivative $\tau^\prime$, and a constant $\ctrano{\tau} \in[0, \infty)$.
nodes.statement_short: Introduces inequality (3) for four points, a differentiable tau and a constant L_tau.

nodes.name: Quadruple inequality with constant L_tau
nodes.statement: \tau(\ol yq) - \tau(\ol yp) - \tau(\ol zq) + \tau(\ol zp) \leq \ctrano{\tau}\, \ol qp \, \tau^\prime(\ol yz)
nodes.label: eq:quadtran

nodes.name: Quadruple inequality
nodes.statement: We call \eqref{eq:quadtran} a \textit{quadruple inequality} \cite{schoetz19} as it establishes a relationship between the six distances among four points, see \cref{fig:fourpoints}.

nodes.name: Identity function tau_1
nodes.statement: If we plug the identity $\tau = \tau_1 := (x\mapsto x)$ and $\ctrano{\tau} = 2$ into \eqref{eq:quadtran}, we obtain \begin{equation} \ol yq - \ol yp - \ol zq + \ol zp \leq 2 \, \ol qp \, . \end{equation}

nodes.name: Quadruple inequality for tau_1
nodes.statement: \ol yq - \ol yp - \ol zq + \ol zp \leq 2 \, \ol qp \, .
nodes.label: eq:quad1

nodes.name: Triangle inequality implies (4)
nodes.statement: The triangle inequality \eqref{eq:tri} implies \eqref{eq:quad1}.
conclusions: The triangle inequality \eqref{eq:tri} implies \eqref{eq:quad1}

nodes.name: (4) implies the triangle inequality in symmetric distance spaces
nodes.statement: Furthermore, in a symmetric distance space $(\mc Q, d)$ \cite{deza16}, where $d$ does not necessarily fulfill the triangle inequality, \eqref{eq:quad1} also implies \eqref{eq:tri} by setting $z=q$.
conclusions: Furthermore, in a symmetric distance space $(\mc Q, d)$ \cite{deza16}, where $d$ does not necessarily fulfill the triangle inequality, \eqref{eq:quad1} also implies \eqref{eq:tri} by setting $z=q$

nodes.name: Square function tau_2
nodes.statement: Next, let us evaluate \eqref{eq:quadtran} with $\tau = \tau_2 :=(x\mapsto x^2)$ and $\ctrano{\tau} = 1$.

nodes.name: tau_2-quadruple inequality (metric Cauchy–Schwarz)
nodes.statement: \ol yq^2 - \ol yp^2 - \ol zq^2 + \ol zp^2 \leq 2\, \ol qp\, \ol yz \, .
nodes.label: eq:quad2

nodes.name: tau_2 quadruple inequality in inner product spaces
Inner-product form of the tau_2 quadruple inequality
nodes.statement: 2 \ip{q-p}{z-y} \leq 2 \normof{q-p}\normof{y-z} \, .

nodes.name: tau_2 quadruple inequality is equivalent to Cauchy–Schwarz in inner product spaces
nodes.statement: Thus, in this case, \eqref{eq:quad2} is equivalent to \eqref{eq:csi}.
conclusions: Thus, in this case, \eqref{eq:quad2} is equivalent to \eqref{eq:csi}

nodes.name: Geodesic metric space
nodes.statement: A geodesic metric space is a metric space such that any two points $q,p\in\mc Q$ can be joined by a geodesic, i.e., a curve of length $\ol qp$.
differentia: any two points $q,p\in\mc Q$ can be joined by a geodesic

nodes.name: Reshetnyak's Quadruple Comparison (four point cosq condition) in CAT(0) spaces
nodes.statement: Equation \eqref{eq:quad2} is well-known to hold in non-positively curved geodesic spaces, which are called $\ms{CAT(0)}$\ spaces or, if they are complete, Hadamard spaces or global NPC spaces.
conclusions: Equation \eqref{eq:quad2} is well-known to hold in non-positively curved geodesic spaces, which are called $\ms{CAT(0)}$\ spaces or, if they are complete, Hadamard spaces or global NPC spaces

nodes.name: Berg–Nikolaev characterization of CAT(0) spaces
nodes.statement: Furthermore, a geodesic space is $\ms{CAT(0)}$\ if it fulfills \eqref{eq:quad2} \cite[Theorem 1]{berg08}.
conclusions: Furthermore, a geodesic space is $\ms{CAT(0)}$\ if it fulfills \eqref{eq:quad2} \cite[Theorem 1]{berg08}

nodes.name: Quadruple inequality for nondecreasing convex functions with concave derivative
nodes.statement: Let $(\mc Q, d)$ be a metric space. Let $y,z,q,p\in\mc Q$. Assume \begin{equation*} \ol yq^2 - \ol yp^2 - \ol zq^2 + \ol zp^2 \leq 2 \, \ol qp\, \ol yz \, . \end{equation*} Let $\tau\colon[0,\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$ be differentiable. Assume $\tau$ is nondecreasing, convex and has a concave derivative $\tau^\prime$. Then \begin{equation} \tau(\ol yq) - \tau(\ol yp) - \tau(\ol zq) + \tau(\ol zp) \leq 2 \, \ol qp \, \tau^\prime(\ol yz)\, . \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: If four points satisfy the tau_2 quadruple (metric Cauchy-Schwarz) inequality, then every nondecreasing convex tau with concave derivative satisfies the tau-quadruple inequality with constant 2.
assumptions: $(\mc Q, d)$ be a metric space
\begin{equation*} \ol yq^2 - \ol yp^2 - \ol zq^2 + \ol zp^2 \leq 2 \, \ol qp\, \ol yz \, . \end{equation*}
$\tau$ is nondecreasing, convex and has a concave derivative $\tau^\prime$
conclusions: \begin{equation} \tau(\ol yq) - \tau(\ol yp) - \tau(\ol zq) + \tau(\ol zp) \leq 2 \, \ol qp \, \tau^\prime(\ol yz)\, . \end{equation}
nodes.label: thm:main

nodes.name: Main quadruple inequality
nodes.statement: \tau(\ol yq) - \tau(\ol yp) - \tau(\ol zq) + \tau(\ol zp) \leq 2 \, \ol qp \, \tau^\prime(\ol yz)\, .
nodes.label: eq:main

nodes.name: Quadruple transformation
nodes.statement: Let $\tau\colon(0,\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$ be differentiable. We call $\tau$ a \textit{quadruple transformation} if there is a constant $\ctrano{\tau}\in[0, \infty)$ such that the following condition holds: For every metric space $(\mc Q, d)$ and pairwise distinct points $y,z,q,p\in\mc Q$ such that \begin{equation*} \ol yq^2 - \ol yp^2 - \ol zq^2 + \ol zp^2 \leq 2\, \ol qp\, \ol yz\, , \end{equation*} we also have \begin{equation*} \tau(\ol yq) - \tau(\ol yp) - \tau(\ol zq) + \tau(\ol zp) \leq \ctrano{\tau}\, \ol qp \, \tau^\prime(\ol yz) \, . \end{equation*} Define the \textit{quadruple constant} of a quadruple transformation $\tau$ as the smallest possible choice of $\ctrano{\tau}$ and denote it as $\ctranobest{\tau}$. Let $\mc{T}$ denote the \textit{set of all quadruple transformations}.
nodes.statement_short: tau is a quadruple transformation if the tau_2 quadruple inequality implies the tau-quadruple inequality with some constant; the smallest constant is the quadruple constant.

nodes.name: Quadruple constant of tau_2 is 1
nodes.statement: Note that $L^*_{\tau_2} = 1$ and $\tau = \tau_2$ in \eqref{eq:quadtran} yields the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality.
conclusions: Note that $L^*_{\tau_2} = 1$ and $\tau = \tau_2$ in \eqref{eq:quadtran} yields the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality

nodes.name: S is contained in T
nodes.statement: Then, by \cref{thm:main}, $\mc S \subseteq \mc{T}$.
conclusions: by \cref{thm:main}, $\mc S \subseteq \mc{T}$

nodes.name: Quadruple constant of tau in S lies in [1, 2]
nodes.statement: We show that, for any $\tau\in\mc S$, the quadruple constant $\ctranobest{\tau}$ is in the interval $[1, 2]$, see \cref{lmm:constLowerBoundOne}.
conclusions: We show that, for any $\tau\in\mc S$, the quadruple constant $\ctranobest{\tau}$ is in the interval $[1, 2]$, see \cref{lmm:constLowerBoundOne}

nodes.name: Set S_0
nodes.statement: Let $\mc S_0$ be set of functions in $\mc S$ with $\tau(0)=0$.

nodes.name: Symmetric quadruple inequality in inner product spaces
nodes.statement: Let $(V, \ip\cdot\cdot)$ be an inner product space with induced metric $d$. Let $y,z,q,p\in V$. Let $\tau\in\mc S_0$. Then \begin{equation} \tau(\ol yq) - \tau(\ol yp) - \tau(\ol zq) + \tau(\ol zp) \leq \tau(\ol qp) + \tau(\ol yz) \, . \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: In inner product spaces, tau in S_0 satisfies the quadruple inequality with symmetric right-hand side tau(qp)+tau(yz).
assumptions: $(V, \ip\cdot\cdot)$ be an inner product space with induced metric $d$
conclusions: \begin{equation} \tau(\ol yq) - \tau(\ol yp) - \tau(\ol zq) + \tau(\ol zp) \leq \tau(\ol qp) + \tau(\ol yz) \, . \end{equation}
nodes.label: thm:ipsymm

nodes.name: Symmetric quadruple inequality
nodes.statement: \tau(\ol yq) - \tau(\ol yp) - \tau(\ol zq) + \tau(\ol zp) \leq \tau(\ol qp) + \tau(\ol yz) \, .
nodes.label: eq:symm:tran

nodes.name: Karamata's inequality
nodes.statement: Let $f \colon \mathbb{R} \to\mathbb{R}$ be a convex and nondecreasing function. Let $a_1,\dots, a_n, b_1\dots, b_n \in \mathbb{R}$ with \begin{equation} \sum_{i=1}^k a_i \leq \sum_{i=1}^k b_i \end{equation} for $k = 1,\dots, n$. Then \begin{equation} \sum_{i=1}^n f(a_i) \leq \sum_{i=1}^n f(b_i) \, . \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Majorized sequences give ordered sums of a convex nondecreasing function.
assumptions: $f \colon \mathbb{R} \to\mathbb{R}$ be a convex and nondecreasing function
conclusions: \begin{equation} \sum_{i=1}^n f(a_i) \leq \sum_{i=1}^n f(b_i) \, . \end{equation}

nodes.name: Majorization condition
nodes.statement: \sum_{i=1}^k a_i \leq \sum_{i=1}^k b_i
nodes.label: eq:majorization

nodes.name: Karamata conclusion
nodes.statement: \sum_{i=1}^n f(a_i) \leq \sum_{i=1}^n f(b_i) \, .

nodes.name: Karamata's inequality proves Theorem 2 in some cases
nodes.statement: If we set $f = \tau$, $n = 4$, $a_1 = \ol yq$, $a_2 = \ol zp$, $a_3 = a_4 = 0$, $b_1 = \ol qp$, $b_2 = \ol yz$, $b_3 = \ol yp$, $b_4 = \ol zq$, then Karamata's inequality proves \cref{thm:ipsymm} for configurations of distances that fulfill \eqref{eq:majorization}. But this does not cover all cases.
nodes.statement_short: With a suitable choice of the a_i and b_i, Karamata's inequality gives Theorem 2 only for configurations satisfying the majorization condition.

nodes.name: Power functions tau_alpha lie in S
nodes.statement: Note that $\tau_\alpha\in\mc S$ for $\alpha\in[1,2]$.
conclusions: Note that $\tau_\alpha\in\mc S$ for $\alpha\in[1,2]$

nodes.name: Metric preserving function
nodes.statement: A function $\varphi\colon[0, \infty)\to[0, \infty)$ is called \textit{metric preserving}, if $\varphi \circ d$ is a metric for any metric space $(\mc Q, d)$.

nodes.name: Euclidean k-point property
nodes.statement: A metric space $(\mc Q, d)$ has the \textit{Euclidean $k$-point property} \cite[Definition 50.1]{blumenthal70} if any $k$-tuple of points in $\mc Q$ has an isometric embedding in the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^{k-1}$.

nodes.name: Euclidean 4-point property implies the tau_2 quadruple inequality
nodes.statement: If $(\mc Q, d)$ has the Euclidean $4$-point property, then \eqref{eq:quad2} is fulfilled.
assumptions: $(\mc Q, d)$ has the Euclidean $4$-point property
conclusions: \eqref{eq:quad2} is fulfilled

nodes.name: Power map phi_gamma
nodes.statement: For $\gamma\in(0, \infty)$, let $\varphi_\gamma(x) := x^\gamma$.

nodes.name: phi_gamma is metric preserving for gamma <= 1
nodes.statement: This function is metric preserving for $\gamma \leq 1$.
conclusions: This function is metric preserving for $\gamma \leq 1$

nodes.name: Blumenthal's theorem on snowflaked metrics
nodes.statement: According to \cite[Theorem 52.1]{blumenthal70}, $(\mc Q, \varphi_\gamma \circ d)$ has the Euclidean $4$-point property for all $\gamma \leq 1/2$. Furthermore, $\gamma = 1/2$ is the largest exponent with this property.
conclusions: According to \cite[Theorem 52.1]{blumenthal70}, $(\mc Q, \varphi_\gamma \circ d)$ has the Euclidean $4$-point property for all $\gamma \leq 1/2$. Furthermore, $\gamma = 1/2$ is the largest exponent with this property

nodes.name: Snowflaked metrics satisfy the tau_2 quadruple inequality
nodes.statement: Thus, $(\mc Q, \varphi_\gamma \circ d)$, fulfills \eqref{eq:quad2} for $\gamma\in(0,1/2]$. In particular, \begin{equation} \ol yq^{2\gamma} - \ol yp^{2\gamma} - \ol yp^{2\gamma} + \ol yp^{2\gamma} \leq 2 \,\ol qp^\gamma \,\ol yz^\gamma \, . \end{equation}
conclusions: Thus, $(\mc Q, \varphi_\gamma \circ d)$, fulfills \eqref{eq:quad2} for $\gamma\in(0,1/2]$. In particular, \begin{equation}\label{eq:symm:blumi} \ol yq^{2\gamma} - \ol yp^{2\gamma} - \ol yp^{2\gamma} + \ol yp^{2\gamma} \leq 2 \,\ol qp^\gamma \,\ol yz^\gamma \, . \end{equation}

nodes.name: Quadruple inequality for snowflaked metric
nodes.statement: \ol yq^{2\gamma} - \ol yp^{2\gamma} - \ol yp^{2\gamma} + \ol yp^{2\gamma} \leq 2 \,\ol qp^\gamma \,\ol yz^\gamma \, .
nodes.label: eq:symm:blumi

nodes.name: Bound via the tau_1 quadruple inequality for d^(2 gamma)
nodes.statement: As $\tilde d = d^{2\gamma}$ is a metric --- $x\mapsto x^{2\gamma}$ is metric preserving for $\gamma\in(0,1/2]$ --- we obtain from \eqref{eq:quad1}, \begin{equation} \ol yq^{2\gamma} - \ol yp^{2\gamma} - \ol yp^{2\gamma} + \ol yp^{2\gamma} \leq 2 \min\brOf{\ol qp^{2\gamma}, \ol yz^{2\gamma}} \, , \end{equation} which also implies \eqref{eq:symm:blumi}.
conclusions: As $\tilde d = d^{2\gamma}$ is a metric --- $x\mapsto x^{2\gamma}$ is metric preserving for $\gamma\in(0,1/2]$ --- we obtain from \eqref{eq:quad1}, \begin{equation} \ol yq^{2\gamma} - \ol yp^{2\gamma} - \ol yp^{2\gamma} + \ol yp^{2\gamma} \leq 2 \min\brOf{\ol qp^{2\gamma}, \ol yz^{2\gamma}} \, , \end{equation} which also implies \eqref{eq:symm:blumi}

nodes.statement: \ol yq^{2\gamma} - \ol yp^{2\gamma} - \ol yp^{2\gamma} + \ol yp^{2\gamma} \leq 2 \min\brOf{\ol qp^{2\gamma}, \ol yz^{2\gamma}} \, ,

nodes.name: CAT(0) 4-point condition
nodes.statement:
A metric space $(\mc Q, d)$ fulfills the $\ms{CAT(0)}$\ $4$-point condition \cite[Definition II.1.10]{bridson99} if, for all $y,z,q,p\in\mc Q$, there are $ ar y, ar z, ar q, ar p\in\mathbb{R}^2$ such that  egin{align*} \ol yq &= 
ormof{ ar y -  ar q}\, , & \ol yp &= 
ormof{ ar y -  ar p}\, , & \ol zq &= 
ormof{ ar z -  ar q}\, , & \ol zp &= 
ormof{ ar z -  ar p}\, , & \ && \ol qp &\leq 
ormof{ ar q -  ar p}\, , & \ol yz &\leq 
ormof{ ar y -  ar z}\, . & && \end{align*}

nodes.name: CAT(0) spaces satisfy the CAT(0) four-point condition
nodes.statement: Every $\ms{CAT(0)}$\ space fulfills the $\ms{CAT(0)}$\ four-point condition, see \cite{reshetnyak68} or \cite[Proposition II.1.11]{bridson99}.
conclusions: Every $\ms{CAT(0)}$\ space fulfills the $\ms{CAT(0)}$\ four-point condition, see \cite{reshetnyak68} or \cite[Proposition II.1.11]{bridson99}

nodes.name: Ptolemaic metric space (Ptolemy's inequality)
nodes.statement: Another famous $4$-point property is \textit{Ptolemy's inequality}: A metric space $(\mc Q, d)$ is called \textit{Ptolemaic} if, for all $y,z, q,p\in\mc Q$, we have \begin{equation} \ol yq \, \ol zp + \ol yp\, \ol zq \leq \ol qp \, \ol yz \, . \end{equation}

nodes.name: Ptolemy's inequality
nodes.statement: \ol yq \, \ol zp + \ol yp\, \ol zq \leq \ol qp \, \ol yz \, .
nodes.label: eq:ptolemy

nodes.name: Inner product spaces are Ptolemaic
nodes.statement: Every inner product space is Ptolemaic.
conclusions: Every inner product space is Ptolemaic

nodes.name: Ptolemaic normed spaces are inner product spaces
nodes.statement: If a normed vector space is Ptolemaic, then it is an inner product space.
assumptions: a normed vector space is Ptolemaic
conclusions: it is an inner product space

nodes.name: CAT(0) spaces are Ptolemaic
nodes.statement: All $\ms{CAT(0)}$\ spaces are Ptolemaic.
conclusions: All $\ms{CAT(0)}$\ spaces are Ptolemaic

nodes.name: Riemannian manifolds: Ptolemaic iff CAT(0)
nodes.statement: A complete Riemannian manifold is Ptolemaic if and only if it is $\ms{CAT(0)}$\ \cite[Theorem 1.1]{buckley09}.
conclusions: A complete Riemannian manifold is Ptolemaic if and only if it is $\ms{CAT(0)}$

nodes.name: Geodesic spaces with the tau_2 quadruple inequality are Ptolemaic
nodes.statement: Each geodesic metric space satisfying the $\tau_2$-quadruple inequality is Ptolemaic, but a geodesic Ptolemaic metric space is not necessarily $\ms{CAT(0)}$\ \cite{foertsch07,berg08}.
conclusions: Each geodesic metric space satisfying the $\tau_2$-quadruple inequality is Ptolemaic, but a geodesic Ptolemaic metric space is not necessarily $\ms{CAT(0)}$\ \cite{foertsch07,berg08}

nodes.name: Roundness exponent
nodes.statement: A value $\alpha\in(0, \infty)$ is called \textit{roundness exponent} of a metric space $(\mc Q, d)$ if, for all $y,z,q,p\in\mc Q$, \begin{equation} \ol yq^\alpha - \ol yp^\alpha - \ol zq^\alpha + \ol zp^\alpha \leq \ol qp^\alpha + \ol yz^\alpha \, . \end{equation}

nodes.name: Roundness inequality
nodes.statement: \ol yq^\alpha - \ol yp^\alpha - \ol zq^\alpha + \ol zp^\alpha \leq \ol qp^\alpha + \ol yz^\alpha \, .
nodes.label: eq:symm:pow

nodes.name: Set of roundness exponents R
nodes.statement: Let $R = R(\mc Q, d)$ be the set of all roundness exponents of $(\mc Q, d)$.

nodes.name: Roundness
nodes.statement: The \textit{roundness} $r = r(\mc Q, d)$ of $(\mc Q, d)$ is the supremum of the roundness exponents $r := \sup R$.

nodes.name: (0,1] consists of roundness exponents
nodes.statement: By the triangle inequality and the metric preserving property of $(x \mapsto x^\alpha)$ for $\alpha \in(0,1]$, we have $(0, 1] \subseteq R$ for all metric spaces.
conclusions: By the triangle inequality and the metric preserving property of $(x \mapsto x^\alpha)$ for $\alpha \in(0,1]$, we have $(0, 1] \subseteq R$ for all metric spaces

nodes.name: Roundness of L_p(0,1)
nodes.statement: The functions spaces $L_p(0,1)$ have roundness $p$ for $p\in[1,2]$ \cite{enflo70lp}.
conclusions: The functions spaces $L_p(0,1)$ have roundness $p$ for $p\in[1,2]$ \cite{enflo70lp}

nodes.name: Roundness 2 characterizes CAT(0) geodesic spaces
nodes.statement: For a geodesic metric space, roundness $r=2$ is equivalent to being $\ms{CAT(0)}$, see \cite[Remark 7]{berg08}.
conclusions: roundness $r=2$ is equivalent to being $\ms{CAT(0)}$

nodes.name: Ultrametric space
nodes.statement: A metric space is called \textit{ultrametric} if the triangle inequality can be strengthened to $\ol yz \leq \max(\ol yp, \ol zp)$ for all points $y,z,p$.

nodes.name: Ultrametric spaces embed isometrically in Hilbert space
nodes.statement: Every ultrametric space can be isometrically embedded in a Hilbert space, see, e.g., \cite[Corollary 5.4]{faver14}.
conclusions: Every ultrametric space can be isometrically embedded in a Hilbert space, see, e.g., \cite[Corollary 5.4]{faver14}

nodes.name: Ultrametric iff infinite roundness
nodes.statement: A metric space is ultrametric if and only if $r = \infty$, \cite[Theorem 5.1]{faver14}.
conclusions: A metric space is ultrametric if and only if $r = \infty$

nodes.name: Roundness exponents of ultrametric spaces
nodes.statement: Then $R = (0, \infty)$, \cite[Proposition 2.7]{faver14}.
conclusions: $R = (0, \infty)$, \cite[Proposition 2.7]{faver14}

nodes.name: R need not be an interval
nodes.statement: In general, $R$ is not necessarily an interval \cite[Remark p.\ 254]{enflo70}.
conclusions: In general, $R$ is not necessarily an interval \cite[Remark p.\ 254]{enflo70}

nodes.name: Roundness exponents of Banach spaces
nodes.statement: But if $(\mc Q, d)$ is a (subset of a) Banach space with the metric $d$ induced by its norm, then $R = (0, r]$ with $r \in [1,2]$, \cite[Proposition 4.1.2]{enflo70}.
assumptions: $(\mc Q, d)$ is a (subset of a) Banach space with the metric $d$ induced by its norm

nodes.name: Roundness inequality in inner product spaces for alpha in (0,2]
nodes.statement: In particular, \eqref{eq:symm:pow} holds for $\alpha\in(0,2]$ in all inner product spaces.
conclusions: In particular, \eqref{eq:symm:pow} holds for $\alpha\in(0,2]$ in all inner product spaces

nodes.name: Additive metric space
nodes.statement: A metric space is called \textit{additive} if \begin{equation} \ol yq + \ol zp \leq \max(\ol yp + \ol zq, \ol qp + \ol yz) \end{equation} for all points $y,z,q,p$.

nodes.name: Additivity condition
nodes.statement: \ol yq + \ol zp \leq \max(\ol yp + \ol zq, \ol qp + \ol yz)

nodes.name: Ultrametric spaces are additive
nodes.statement: Every ultrametric space is additive.
conclusions: Every ultrametric space is additive

nodes.name: Additive spaces are Ptolemaic
nodes.statement: Every additive metric space is Ptolemaic.
conclusions: Every additive metric space is Ptolemaic

nodes.name: Additive spaces have roundness at least 2
nodes.statement: Additive metric spaces have roundness $r \geq 2$ \cite[Proposition 4.1]{faver14}.
conclusions: Additive metric spaces have roundness $r \geq 2$ \cite[Proposition 4.1]{faver14}

nodes.name: Topchii–Vatutin inequality
nodes.statement: For a suitably integrable martingale $(M_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}_0}$, we have \begin{equation} \mathbb{E}\expectarg{\tau(\abs{M_n}) - \tau(\abs{M_0})} \leq 2 \sum_{k=1}^n \mathbb{E}\expectarg{\tau(\abs{M_k-M_{k-1}})} \end{equation} for all $\tau\in\mc S_0$, where $\mathbb{E}\expectarg{\cdot}$ denotes the expectation.
nodes.statement_short: For tau in S_0 the tau-increment of a martingale is bounded by twice the sum of expected tau of its increments.
conclusions: For a suitably integrable martingale $(M_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}_0}$, we have \begin{equation} \mathbb{E}\expectarg{\tau(\abs{M_n}) - \tau(\abs{M_0})} \leq 2 \sum_{k=1}^n \mathbb{E}\expectarg{\tau(\abs{M_k-M_{k-1}})} \end{equation} for all $\tau\in\mc S_0$, where $\mathbb{E}\expectarg{\cdot}$ denotes the expectation

nodes.name: Topchii–Vatutin bound

nodes.name: Topchii–Vatutin Lemma 6
nodes.statement: Let $\tau \in \mc S_0$. For $a,b\in[0, \infty)$ with $a\geq b$, it was shown that $\tau(a+b) + \tau(a-b) \leq 2 \tau(a) + 2 \tau(b)$.
conclusions: $\tau(a+b) + \tau(a-b) \leq 2 \tau(a) + 2 \tau(b)$

nodes.name: Fréchet mean
nodes.statement: If $Y$ is a random variable with values in a metric space $(\mc Q, d)$, the Fréchet mean is $arg\,min_{q\in\mc Q}\mathbb{E}\expectarg{\ol Yq^2}$, where we assume $\mathbb{E}\expectarg{\ol Yq^2}<\infty$ for all $q\in\mc Q$.

nodes.name: Fréchet median and tau-Fréchet mean
nodes.statement: Similarly, one can define the Fréchet median \cite{fletcher09} as $arg\,min_{q\in\mc Q}\mathbb{E}\expectarg{\ol Yq}$, or a more general $\tau$-Fréchet mean \cite{schoetz22} as $arg\,min_{q\in\mc Q}\mathbb{E}\expectarg{\tau(\ol Yq)}$ for functions $\tau\colon[0, \infty)\to\mathbb{R}$.

nodes.name: Huber, Pseudo-Huber and log-cosh losses
nodes.statement: Noteworthy examples of $\tau\in\mc S$ in this context, aside from $\tau = \tau_\alpha$, are the Huber loss $\tau_{\ms H,\delta}$ \cite{huber64} and the Pseudo-Huber loss $\tau_{\ms{pH},\delta}$ \cite{charbonnier94} for $\delta\in(0, \infty)$, \begin{align*} \tau_{\ms H,\delta}(x) &:= \begin{cases} \frac12 x^2 & \text{ for } x \leq \delta\, ,\\ \delta(x - \frac12 \delta) & \text{ for } x > \delta\, ,\\ \end{cases} & \tau_{\ms{pH},\delta}(x) &:= \delta^2 \br{\sqrt{1 + \frac{x^2}{\delta^2}} - 1} \, , \end{align*} as well as $x\mapsto \ln(\cosh(x))$ \cite{green90}.
nodes.statement_short: Huber loss, Pseudo-Huber loss and ln(cosh(x)) are examples of functions in S.

nodes.name: Proof of Well-definedness of the quadruple constant
nodes.statement: Let $\tau\in\mc{T}$. Let $(L_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}\subseteq[0, \infty)$ be a decreasing sequence with $L_\infty := \lim_{n\to\infty} L_n$. Assume \eqref{eq:quadtran} is true for all $\ctrano{\tau} = L_n$. We need to show that \eqref{eq:quadtran} is also true for $\ctrano{\tau} = L_\infty$. If it were false, there would be a metric space $(\mc Q, d)$ with points $y,z,q,p\in\mc Q$ such that \begin{equation} \tau(\ol yq) - \tau(\ol yp) - \tau(\ol zq) + \tau(\ol zp) > L_\infty\, \ol qp \, \tau^\prime(\ol yz) \, . \end{equation} As the inequality is strict, it would also hold when $L_\infty$ is replaced by a $L_n$ for a sufficiently large $n$, which is a contradiction.

nodes.name: Proof of Lower bounds on the quadruple constant
nodes.statement: For all parts, we apply \eqref{eq:quadtran} in the metric space of the real line with Euclidean metric, see \cref{fig:quadriProofLower}. \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item Set $z=q=0$, $y=u$, $p = u/2$. Then \eqref{eq:quadtran} becomes \begin{equation*} \tau(u) - \tau(0) \leq \ctrano{\tau} \frac u2 \tau^\prime(u) \, . \end{equation*} \item Set $z=q=0$, $y=u$, $p = 2u$. Then \eqref{eq:quadtran} becomes \begin{equation*} \tau(2u) - \tau(0) \leq 2 \ctrano{\tau} u \tau^\prime(u) \, . \end{equation*} \item Let $\varepsilon\in(0, \min(u,v))$. Set $q = 0$, $p = \varepsilon$, $y = u$, $z = v$. Then \eqref{eq:quadtran} becomes \begin{align*} \tau(u) - \tau(u-\varepsilon) - \tau(v) + \tau(v-\varepsilon) \leq \ctrano{\tau}\, \varepsilon \, \tau^\prime(\abs{u-v}) \, . \end{align*} Thus, \begin{align*} \ctrano{\tau} \tau^\prime(\abs{u-v}) \geq \frac{\tau(u) - \tau(u-\varepsilon)}{\varepsilon} -\frac{\tau(v) - \tau(v-\varepsilon)}{\varepsilon} \xrightarrow{\varepsilon \to 0} \tau^\prime(u) - \tau^\prime(v) \, . \end{align*} \item Let $\varepsilon\in(0, \min(u,v))$. Let $q = 0$, $p = \varepsilon$, $y = u$, $z = -v$. Then \eqref{eq:quadtran} becomes \begin{align*} \tau(u) - \tau(u-\varepsilon) - \tau(v) + \tau(v+\varepsilon) \leq \ctrano{\tau}\, \varepsilon \, \tau^\prime(u+v) \, . \end{align*} Thus, \begin{align*} \ctrano{\tau} \tau^\prime(u+v) \geq \frac{\tau(u) - \tau(u-\varepsilon)}{\varepsilon} + \frac{\tau(v+\varepsilon) - \tau(v)}{\varepsilon} \xrightarrow{\varepsilon \to 0} \tau^\prime(u) + \tau^\prime(v) \, . \end{align*} \end{enumerate}

nodes.name: Proof of Quadruple constant is at least one
nodes.statement: Let $u\in(0, \infty)$ be such that $\tau^\prime(u) \neq 0$. Then \cref{lmm:nondecreasing} \ref{lmm:nondecreasing:incr} implies $\tau^\prime(u) > 0$. Let $\varepsilon\in(0, u)$. In the metric space of the real line with Euclidean metric, we choose $z = q = 0$, $p = \varepsilon$, $y = u$, see \cref{fig:quadriProofOne}. Then \eqref{eq:quadtran} becomes \begin{align*} \tau(u) - \tau(u-\varepsilon) - \tau(0) + \tau(\varepsilon) \leq \ctrano{\tau}\, \varepsilon \, \tau^\prime(u) \, . \end{align*} As $\tau$ is nondecreasing by \cref{lmm:nondecreasing} \ref{lmm:nondecreasing:incr}, we have $\tau(0) = \lim_{x\searrow0} \tau(x) \leq \tau(\varepsilon)$. Thus, \begin{align*} \ctrano{\tau} \tau^\prime(u) \geq \frac{\tau(u) - \tau(u-\varepsilon)}{\varepsilon} \xrightarrow{\varepsilon \to 0} \tau^\prime(u) \, . \end{align*}

nodes.name: Limits of quadruple transformations
nodes.statement: Let $(\tau_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}\subseteq\mc{T}$ with constants $(\ctrano{\tau_n})_{n\in\mathbb{N}}\subseteq[0, \infty)$. Let $\tau\colon(0, \infty)\to\mathbb{R}$ be a differentiable function. Assume $\lim_{n\to\infty}\tau_n(x) = \tau(x)$ and $\limsup_{n\to\infty} \tau^\prime_n(x) \leq \tau^\prime(x)$ for all $x\in(0, \infty)$. Set $\ctrano{\tau} := \limsup_{n\to\infty} \ctrano{\tau_n}$. Assume $\ctrano{\tau} < \infty$. Then $\tau\in\mc{T}$ with constant $\ctrano{\tau}$.
conclusions: $\tau\in\mc{T}$ with constant $\ctrano{\tau}$
nodes.label: lmm:quad:limit

nodes.name: Proof of Limits of quadruple transformations
nodes.statement: This is a direct consequence of the assumed limit properties of $\tau$, $\tau^\prime$, and $\ctrano{\tau}$, and of the quadruple inequality for $\tau_n$ with constant $\ctrano{\tau_n}$: \begin{align*} \tau(\ol yq) - \tau(\ol yp) - \tau(\ol zq) + \tau(\ol zp) &= \lim_{n\to\infty} \br{\tau_n(\ol yq) - \tau_n(\ol yp) - \tau_n(\ol zq) + \tau_n(\ol zp)} \\&\leq \lim_{n\to\infty} \ctrano{\tau_n}\,\ol qp\, \tau^\prime_n(\ol yz) \\&\leq \ctrano{\tau} \,\ol qp\, \tau^\prime(\ol yz) \, . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Pass to the limit in the quadruple inequalities of tau_n.

Then $(x\mapsto \tau(x)+\tilde\tau(x)) \in \mc{T}$ with constant $\ctrano{\tau} + \ctrano{\tilde\tau}$. \end{enumerate}

nodes.name: Set S of nondecreasing convex functions with concave derivative
nodes.statement: We define $\mc S$ to be the set of nondecreasing convex functions $\tau\colon[0, \infty)\to\mathbb{R}$ that are differentiable on $(0, \infty)$ with concave derivative $\tau^\prime$.

also_stated_at: Let $\mc S$ be the set of all nondecreasing, convex, and differentiable functions $\tau\colon[0,\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$ with concave derivative.

nodes.name: Derivative at 0
nodes.statement: We extend the domain of $\tau^\prime$ to $[0, \infty)$ by setting $\tau^\prime(0) := \lim_{x\searrow0} \tau^\prime(x)$, which exists as $\tau^\prime$ is nonnegative and nondecreasing.

nodes.name: Right derivative
nodes.statement: Let $I\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ be convex. Let $t_0\in I$ with $t_0<\sup I$. For a function $f\colon I \to \mathbb{R}$ the \textit{right derivative} at $t_0$ is defined as \begin{equation} \partial_+ f(t_0) = \lim_{t\searrow t}\frac{f(t)-f(t_0)}{t-t_0} \end{equation} if the limit exits.

nodes.name: Simple properties of functions in S
nodes.statement: Let $\tau\in\mc S$. \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item Then $\tau$ is continuous; its right derivative at $0$ exits and $\partial_+ \tau(0) = \tau^\prime(0)$; $\tau^\prime$ is nonnegative, nondecreasing, and continuous. \item Assume $\tau\in\setccd{2}$. Then $\tau^{\prime\prime}$ is nonnegative and nonincreasing. \item Assume $\tau\in\setccd{3}$. Then $\tau^{\prime\prime\prime}$ is nonpositive. \end{enumerate}
conclusions: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item Then $\tau$ is continuous; its right derivative at $0$ exits and $\partial_+ \tau(0) = \tau^\prime(0)$; $\tau^\prime$ is nonnegative, nondecreasing, and continuous. \item Assume $\tau\in\setccd{2}$. Then $\tau^{\prime\prime}$ is nonnegative and nonincreasing. \item Assume $\tau\in\setccd{3}$. Then $\tau^{\prime\prime\prime}$ is nonpositive. \end{enumerate}

nodes.name: Polynomial bounds
nodes.statement: \mbox{ } Let $\tau\in\setccd3$. Let $x, y \in [0, \infty)$. Then \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item \begin{equation*} \tau(x) + y \tau^\prime(x) \leq \tau(x + y) \leq \tau(x) + y \tau^\prime(x) + \frac12 y^2 \tau^{\prime\prime}(x) \, , \end{equation*} \item \begin{equation*} \tau^\prime(x) \leq \tau^\prime(x + y) \leq \tau^\prime(x) + y \tau^{\prime\prime}(x) \, . \end{equation*} \end{enumerate}
conclusions: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item \begin{equation*} \tau(x) + y \tau^\prime(x) \leq \tau(x + y) \leq \tau(x) + y \tau^\prime(x) + \frac12 y^2 \tau^{\prime\prime}(x) \, , \end{equation*} \item \begin{equation*} \tau^\prime(x) \leq \tau^\prime(x + y) \leq \tau^\prime(x) + y \tau^{\prime\prime}(x) \, . \end{equation*} \end{enumerate}
nodes.label: lmm:ccpoly

nodes.name: Difference bound
nodes.statement: Let $\tau\in\mc S$. \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item Let $x,y\in[0, \infty)$. Assume $x \geq y$. Then \begin{equation*} \frac{x-y}2\br{\tau^\prime(x)+\tau^\prime(y)} \leq \tau(x) - \tau(y) \leq (x-y)\tau^\prime\brOf{\frac{x+y}{2}} \, . \end{equation*} \item Let $x,y\in[0, \infty)$. Then \begin{equation*} \tau(x+y) - \tau(\abs{x-y}) \leq 2\min(x, y)\tau^\prime(\max(x, y)) \, . \end{equation*} \end{enumerate}
conclusions: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item Let $x,y\in[0, \infty)$. Assume $x \geq y$. Then \begin{equation*} \frac{x-y}2\br{\tau^\prime(x)+\tau^\prime(y)} \leq \tau(x) - \tau(y) \leq (x-y)\tau^\prime\brOf{\frac{x+y}{2}} \, . \end{equation*} \item Let $x,y\in[0, \infty)$. Then \begin{equation*} \tau(x+y) - \tau(\abs{x-y}) \leq 2\min(x, y)\tau^\prime(\max(x, y)) \, . \end{equation*} \end{enumerate}
nodes.label: lmm:ccdiff

nodes.name: Smooth approximation
nodes.statement: Let $\tau\in\mc S$. Then there is a sequence $(\tau_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}\subseteq \setccd{\infty}$ such that $\tau(x) =\lim_{n\to\infty}\tau_n(x)$ and $\tau^\prime(x) =\lim_{n\to\infty}\tau^\prime_n(x)$.
conclusions: there is a sequence $(\tau_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}\subseteq \setccd{\infty}$ such that $\tau(x) =\lim_{n\to\infty}\tau_n(x)$ and $\tau^\prime(x) =\lim_{n\to\infty}\tau^\prime_n(x)$
nodes.label: lmm:cc:molli

nodes.name: Proof of Smooth approximation
nodes.statement: We will smooth $\tau^\prime$ by convolution with a mollifier. The convolution is executed in the group of positive real numbers under multiplication endowed with its Haar measure $\mu(A) = \int_A \frac1x \mathrm{d} x$ for $A\subseteq(0, \infty)$ measurable. For $n\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\varphi_n\in\setd\infty((0, \infty))$ be a sequence of nonnegative functions with support in $[\exp(-1/n), \exp(1/n)]$ and \begin{equation} \int_0^\infty \frac{\varphi_n(x)} x \mathrm{d} x = 1\, . \end{equation} Let $\tau\in\mc S$ with derivative $\tau^\prime$. For $n\in\mathbb{N}$, $x\in[0, \infty)$, we define \begin{equation} \tau_n(x) := \tau(0) + \int_{0}^x \int_{0}^\infty \frac{\varphi_n(z)}{z} \tau^\prime\brOf{\frac yz} \mathrm{d} z \mathrm{d} y \, . \end{equation} Then, for $y\in[0, \infty)$, \begin{equation} \tau^\prime_n(y) = \int_{0}^\infty \frac{\varphi_n(z)}{z} \tau^\prime\brOf{\frac yz} \mathrm{d} z = \int_{\mathbb{R}} \varphi_n(\mathrm{e}^t) \tau^\prime\brOf{\mathrm{e}^{\log(y) - t}} \mathrm{d} t \, . \end{equation} Thus, $s\mapsto \tau^\prime_n(\mathrm{e}^s)$ is the convolution of $t\mapsto \varphi_n(\mathrm{e}^t)$ with $t\mapsto\tau^\prime\brOf{\mathrm{e}^t}$. Using standard results on convolutions, the mollified function has following properties: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item $\tau^\prime_n$ is infinitely differentiable on $(0, \infty)$, because $\varphi_n$ is, \item $\tau^\prime_n$ is nonnegative, nondecreasing, and concave, because $\tau^\prime$ is and $\varphi_n$ is nonnegative, \item $\lim_{n\to\infty}\tau^\prime_n(x) = \tau^\prime(x)$ because $\tau^\prime$ is continuous. \end{enumerate} Furthermore, $\tau_n$ is convex, as $\tau^\prime_n$ is nondecreasing and $\lim_{n\to\infty}\tau_n(x) = \tau(x)$ by dominated convergence. Thus, $(\tau_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}} \subseteq \setccd{\infty}$, and the sequence has the desired point-wise limits.
nodes.statement_short: Mollify tau' by multiplicative convolution and integrate. Convolution preserves nonnegativity, monotonicity and concavity of tau'.

nodes.statement_short: (iii) tau_n' -> tau' pointwise

nodes.name: tau_n is convex and converges to tau, so tau_n lie in S^infinity
nodes.statement: Furthermore, $\tau_n$ is convex, as $\tau^\prime_n$ is nondecreasing and $\lim_{n\to\infty}\tau_n(x) = \tau(x)$ by dominated convergence. Thus, $(\tau_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}} \subseteq \setccd{\infty}$, and the sequence has the desired point-wise limits.
nodes.statement_short: tau_n is convex and converges to tau, so tau_n lie in S^infinity

nodes.name: S is closed under pointwise limits
nodes.statement: Let $(\tau_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}\subseteq\mc S$. Let $\tau\colon[0, \infty)\to\mathbb{R}$ be differentiable. Assume that $\tau(x) = \lim_{n\to\infty}\tau_n(x)$ for all $x\in[0, \infty)$. Then $\tau\in\mc S$.
conclusions: $\tau\in\mc S$

nodes.name: Proof of S is closed under pointwise limits
nodes.statement: As $\tau_n$ is nondecreasing and convex, so is $\tau$. As $\tau^\prime_n$ is concave, by \cite[Theorem 25.7]{rockafellar70}, for all $x\in(0, \infty)$, \begin{equation} \lim_{n\to\infty} \tau^\prime_n(x) = \tau^\prime(x) \, . \end{equation} Thus, as all $\tau^\prime_n$ are concave, $\tau^\prime$ is concave on $(0, \infty)$. As $\tau$ is convex, $\frac{\tau(x+h)-\tau(x)}{h}$ is increasing in both $x$ and $h$. Thus, \begin{align*} \liminf_{x\searrow0} \tau^\prime(x) &= \inf_{x\in(0, \infty)} \tau^\prime(x) \\&= \inf_{x,h\in(0, \infty)} \frac{\tau(x+h)-\tau(x)}{h} \\&= \liminf_{h\searrow0} \frac{\tau(h)-\tau(0)}{h} \\&= \tau^\prime(0) \, . \end{align*} Therefore, $\tau^\prime$ is continuous at $0$ and concavity extends to $[0, \infty)$.
nodes.statement_short: Pointwise limits keep convexity/monotonicity; Rockafellar's theorem gives convergence of derivatives and concavity of tau'.

nodes.name: tau inherits monotonicity and convexity
nodes.statement: As $\tau_n$ is nondecreasing and convex, so is $\tau$.
nodes.statement_short: tau inherits monotonicity and convexity

nodes.name: Rockafellar's Theorem 25.7 gives tau_n' -> tau', so tau' is concave
nodes.statement: As $\tau^\prime_n$ is concave, by \cite[Theorem 25.7]{rockafellar70}, for all $x\in(0, \infty)$, \begin{equation} \lim_{n\to\infty} \tau^\prime_n(x) = \tau^\prime(x) \, . \end{equation} Thus, as all $\tau^\prime_n$ are concave, $\tau^\prime$ is concave on $(0, \infty)$.
nodes.statement_short: Rockafellar's Theorem 25.7 gives tau_n' -> tau', so tau' is concave

nodes.name: Convergence of derivatives
nodes.statement: \lim_{n\to\infty} \tau^\prime_n(x) = \tau^\prime(x) \, .

nodes.name: Monotone difference quotients identify the infimum of tau' with tau'(0): continuity and co
nodes.statement: As $\tau$ is convex, $\frac{\tau(x+h)-\tau(x)}{h}$ is increasing in both $x$ and $h$. Thus, \begin{align*} \liminf_{x\searrow0} \tau^\prime(x) &= \inf_{x\in(0, \infty)} \tau^\prime(x) \\&= \inf_{x,h\in(0, \infty)} \frac{\tau(x+h)-\tau(x)}{h} \\&= \liminf_{h\searrow0} \frac{\tau(h)-\tau(0)}{h} \\&= \tau^\prime(0) \, . \end{align*} Therefore, $\tau^\prime$ is continuous at $0$ and concavity extends to $[0, \infty)$.
nodes.statement_short: Monotone difference quotients identify the infimum of tau' with tau'(0): continuity and concavity on [0, infinity)

nodes.name: S is closed under nonnegative linear combinations
nodes.statement: \mbox{ } \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item Let $\tau\in\mc S$. Let $a\in[0, \infty)$. Then $(x\mapsto a\tau(x)) \in \mc S$. \item Let $\tau, \tilde \tau\in \mc S$. Then $(x\mapsto \tau(x)+\tilde\tau(x)) \in \mc S$. \end{enumerate}
conclusions: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item Let $\tau\in\mc S$. Let $a\in[0, \infty)$. Then $(x\mapsto a\tau(x)) \in \mc S$. \item Let $\tau, \tilde \tau\in \mc S$. Then $(x\mapsto \tau(x)+\tilde\tau(x)) \in \mc S$. \end{enumerate}

nodes.name: Proof of S is closed under nonnegative linear combinations
nodes.statement: Both parts follow directly from the definition of $\mc S$ and linearity of the derivative operator.

nodes.name: Parametrization
nodes.statement: We refer to this representation as a \textit{parametrization}.

nodes.name: 3-point parametrization
nodes.statement: \mbox{ } \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item Let $(\mc Q, d)$ be a metric space and $y,q,p\in\mc Q$. Set $a := \ol yp$ and $b:= \ol qp$. Isometrically embed $y,q,p$ in the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ and set $s := \cos(\measuredangle ypq)$ with the angle $\measuredangle ypq$ measured in the Euclidean plane. Then, $\ol yq^2 = a^2 + b^2 - 2 s ab$ and $a,b\in[0, \infty), s \in[-1, 1]$. \item For all $a,b\in[0, \infty), s \in[-1, 1]$ there is a metric space with a triplet of points $y,q,p$ such that $\ol yp = a$, $\ol qp = b$, and $\ol yq^2 = a^2 + b^2 - 2 s ab$. \end{enumerate}
conclusions: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item Let $(\mc Q, d)$ be a metric space and $y,q,p\in\mc Q$. Set $a := \ol yp$ and $b:= \ol qp$. Isometrically embed $y,q,p$ in the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ and set $s := \cos(\measuredangle ypq)$ with the angle $\measuredangle ypq$ measured in the Euclidean plane. Then, $\ol yq^2 = a^2 + b^2 - 2 s ab$ and $a,b\in[0, \infty), s \in[-1, 1]$. \item For all $a,b\in[0, \infty), s \in[-1, 1]$ there is a metric space with a triplet of points $y,q,p$ such that $\ol yp = a$, $\ol qp = b$, and $\ol yq^2 = a^2 + b^2 - 2 s ab$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.label: lmm:threepoint

nodes.name: Proof of 3-point parametrization
nodes.statement: The first part is true by construction. For given parameters $a,b\in[0, \infty), s \in[-1, 1]$, we can easily construct a triangle in $\mathbb{R}^2$ with sides $a, b, \sqrt{a^2 + b^2 - 2 s ab}$ and an angle $\arccos(s)$ between the sides with length $a$ and $b$. The corners of this triangle are the points $y,q,p$.
nodes.statement_short: Construct a Euclidean triangle with the prescribed sides and angle.

nodes.name: Part (i) holds by construction

nodes.name: 4-point parametrization
nodes.statement: \mbox{ } \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item Let $(\mc Q, d)$ be a metric space and $y,z,q,p\in\mc Q$. Set $a:=\ol zp$, $c:=\ol yp$, $b:=\ol qp$, $s := \cos(\measuredangle ypq)$, $r := \cos(\measuredangle zpq)$, $t := \cos(\measuredangle ypz)$, with all angles measured as in an isometric $3$-point embedding in the Euclidean plane. Then, \begin{align*} \ol yz^2 &= a^2 + c^2 - 2tac\, , & \ol yq^2 &= c^2 + b^2 - 2scb\, , & \ol zq^2 &= a^2 + b^2 - 2rab \, . \end{align*} Furthermore, $a,b,c\in[0, \infty)$, $r,s,t\in[-1, 1]$, and \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} -tac &\leq b^2 - rab - scb + \sqrt{a^2 - 2rab + b^2}\sqrt{c^2 - 2scb + b^2}\, ,\\ -rab &\leq c^2 - tac - scb + \sqrt{a^2 - 2tac + c^2}\sqrt{c^2 - 2scb + b^2}\, ,\\ -scb &\leq a^2 - rab - tac + \sqrt{a^2 - 2rab + b^2}\sqrt{a^2 - 2tac + c^2}\, . \end{aligned} \end{equation} \item For all $a,b,c\in[0, \infty)$, $r,s,t\in[-1, 1]$ that fulfill \eqref{lmm:fourpoint:trianlge}, there is a metric space $(\mc Q, d)$ with a quadruple of points $y,z,q,p\in\mc Q$ such that \begin{align*} a &= \ol zp\, , & c &= \ol yp\, , & b &= \ol qp\, , \\ \ol yz^2 &= a^2 + c^2 - 2tac\, , & \ol yq^2 &= c^2 + b^2 - 2scb\, , & \ol zq^2 &= a^2 + b^2 - 2rab \, . \end{align*} \end{enumerate}
conclusions: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item Let $(\mc Q, d)$ be a metric space and $y,z,q,p\in\mc Q$. Set $a:=\ol zp$, $c:=\ol yp$, $b:=\ol qp$, $s := \cos(\measuredangle ypq)$, $r := \cos(\measuredangle zpq)$, $t := \cos(\measuredangle ypz)$, with all angles measured as in an isometric $3$-point embedding in the Euclidean plane. Then, \begin{align*} \ol yz^2 &= a^2 + c^2 - 2tac\, , & \ol yq^2 &= c^2 + b^2 - 2scb\, , & \ol zq^2 &= a^2 + b^2 - 2rab \, . \end{align*} Furthermore, $a,b,c\in[0, \infty)$, $r,s,t\in[-1, 1]$, and \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} -tac &\leq b^2 - rab - scb + \sqrt{a^2 - 2rab + b^2}\sqrt{c^2 - 2scb + b^2}\, ,\\ -rab &\leq c^2 - tac - scb + \sqrt{a^2 - 2tac + c^2}\sqrt{c^2 - 2scb + b^2}\, ,\\ -scb &\leq a^2 - rab - tac + \sqrt{a^2 - 2rab + b^2}\sqrt{a^2 - 2tac + c^2}\, . \end{aligned} \end{equation} \item For all $a,b,c\in[0, \infty)$, $r,s,t\in[-1, 1]$ that fulfill \eqref{lmm:fourpoint:trianlge}, there is a metric space $(\mc Q, d)$ with a quadruple of points $y,z,q,p\in\mc Q$ such that \begin{align*} a &= \ol zp\, , & c &= \ol yp\, , & b &= \ol qp\, , \\ \ol yz^2 &= a^2 + c^2 - 2tac\, , & \ol yq^2 &= c^2 + b^2 - 2scb\, , & \ol zq^2 &= a^2 + b^2 - 2rab \, . \end{align*} \end{enumerate}
nodes.label: lmm:fourpoint

nodes.name: Triangle constraints of the 4-point parametrization
nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} -tac &\leq b^2 - rab - scb + \sqrt{a^2 - 2rab + b^2}\sqrt{c^2 - 2scb + b^2}\, ,\\ -rab &\leq c^2 - tac - scb + \sqrt{a^2 - 2tac + c^2}\sqrt{c^2 - 2scb + b^2}\, ,\\ -scb &\leq a^2 - rab - tac + \sqrt{a^2 - 2rab + b^2}\sqrt{a^2 - 2tac + c^2}\, . \end{aligned}
nodes.label: lmm:fourpoint:trianlge

nodes.name: Proof of 4-point parametrization
nodes.statement: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item The inequalities \eqref{lmm:fourpoint:trianlge} are due to the triangle inequality, \begin{equation*} \ol yz \leq \ol yq + \ol zq \, ,\qquad \ol zq \leq \ol yz + \ol yq \, ,\qquad \ol yq \leq \ol yz + \ol zq \, . \end{equation*} \item Define a four point set $\mc Q$ with elements named $y,z,q,p$. Define $d\colon\mc Q\times \mc Q\to[0, \infty)$ with the equations given in the lemma, extended by symmetry and $d(x,x) = 0$ for all $x\in\mc Q$. By construction, $d$ is a semimetric \cite{deza16} (vanishing distance for non-identical points allowed) so that identifying points with distance 0 yields a metric space. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Triangle inequality for (i); define a semimetric on four points for (ii).

nodes.name: Shorthand tau_sqrt and parametrized inequalities
nodes.statement: With this parametrization and \begin{equation} a^2 - c^2 - (a^2-2rab+b^2) + (c^2-2scb+b^2) = 2b \br{ra-sc} \, , \end{equation} \eqref{eq:quad2} can be expressed as \begin{equation} b \br{ra-sc} \leq b \sqrt{a^2 + c^2 - 2tac}\, , \end{equation} and \eqref{eq:quadtran} becomes \begin{equation} \tau(a) - \tau(c) - \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}\brOf{a^2-2rab+b^2} + \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}\brOf{c^2-2scb+b^2} \leq \ctrano{\tau} \, b \, \tau^\prime(a^2 + c^2 - 2tac)\, , \end{equation} where we use the shorthand $\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(x) := \tau(\sqrt x)$.
nodes.statement_short: In the 4-point parametrization the tau_2 condition and the quadruple inequality take forms (eq:quad2:param), (eq:quadtran:param); tau_sqrt(x) := tau(sqrt x).

nodes.name: Parametrized quadruple inequality

nodes.name: Strong quadruple inequality
nodes.statement: Let $\tau\in\mc S$. Let $(\mc Q, d)$ be a metric space. Let $y,z,q,p\in\mc Q$. Assume, there is $\ctrano{}\in[2,\infty)$ such that \begin{equation} \ol yq^2 - \ol yp^2 - \ol zq^2 + \ol zp^2 \leq \ctrano{} \, \ol qp\, \ol yz \, . \end{equation} Then \begin{equation} \tau(\ol yq) - \tau(\ol yp) - \tau(\ol zq) + \tau(\ol zp) \leq \ctrano{} \, \ol qp \, \tau^\prime\brOf{\ol yz}\, . \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: The quadruple inequality with any constant L >= 2 in both the assumption and the conclusion.
conclusions: \label{thm:strong} Let $\tau\in\mc S$. Let $(\mc Q, d)$ be a metric space. Let $y,z,q,p\in\mc Q$. Assume, there is $\ctrano{}\in[2,\infty)$ such that \begin{equation}\label{eq:strong:assu} \ol yq^2 - \ol yp^2 - \ol zq^2 + \ol zp^2 \leq \ctrano{} \, \ol qp\, \ol yz \, . \end{equation} Then \begin{equation}\label{eq:strong} \tau(\ol yq) - \tau(\ol yp) - \tau(\ol zq) + \tau(\ol zp) \leq \ctrano{} \, \ol qp \, \tau^\prime\brOf{\ol yz}\, . \end{equation}
nodes.label: thm:strong

nodes.name: Strong quadruple inequality

nodes.name: Proof of Strong quadruple inequality
nodes.statement: Let $\tau \in \setccod3$. Using \eqref{eq:quad2lhs:simplification}, the metric version of \eqref{eq:thm:main:param} is \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} &\tau(\ol yq) - \tau(\ol yp) - \tau(\ol zq) + \tau(\ol zp) \\&\leq 2 \,\ol qp\, \tau^\prime\brOf{\max\brOf{\frac{\ol yq^2 - \ol yp^2 - \ol zq^2 + \ol zp^2}{2 \,\ol qp}, |\ol zp - \ol yp|}} \, . \end{aligned} \end{equation} Using \eqref{eq:strong:assu} and the triangle inequality, we bound the right-hand side of \eqref{eq:strong:proof:1}, by \begin{equation} 2 \,\ol qp\, \tau^\prime\brOf{\max\brOf{\frac{\ctrano{} \, \ol yz}{2}, \ol yz}}\, . \end{equation} With \cref{lmm:tranconcave} \ref{lmm:tranconcave:factor} and $\ctrano{}/2\geq 1$, we obtain \eqref{eq:strong}. To extend the result shown for $\tau\in\setccod3$ to $\tau\in\mc S$, we use \cref{lmm:cc:molli} and \cref{lmm:quad:limit} to remove the smoothness requirement, and \cref{lmm:quadconst} \ref{lmm:quadconst:constisquad} and \cref{lmm:quadstablin} \ref{lmm:quadstablin:add} to remove the requirement $\tau(0) = 0$.

conclusions: Thus, assuming \begin{equation} \abs{\ol yq^2 - \ol yp^2 - \ol zq^2 + \ol zp^2} \leq 2\, \ol qp \, \ol yz \end{equation} we get \begin{equation} \abs{\tau(\ol yq) - \tau(\ol yp) - \tau(\ol zq) + \tau(\ol zp)} \leq 2 \min(\ol qp\,\tau^\prime(\ol yz), \ol yz\, \tau^\prime(\ol qp)) \, . \end{equation}

nodes.name: Two-sided tau_2 condition
nodes.statement: \abs{\ol yq^2 - \ol yp^2 - \ol zq^2 + \ol zp^2} \leq 2\, \ol qp \, \ol yz

nodes.name: Two-sided quadruple inequality
nodes.statement: \abs{\tau(\ol yq) - \tau(\ol yp) - \tau(\ol zq) + \tau(\ol zp)} \leq 2 \min(\ol qp\,\tau^\prime(\ol yz), \ol yz\, \tau^\prime(\ol qp)) \, .

nodes.name: Bounds for the right-hand side
nodes.statement: Let $\tau\in\mc S_0$. Let $(\mc Q, d)$ be a metric space. Let $y,z,q,p\in\mc Q$. Assume \begin{equation} \ol yq^2 - \ol yp^2 - \ol zq^2 + \ol zp^2 \leq 2\, \ol qp \, \ol yz \, . \end{equation} Then the value \begin{equation} \tau(\ol yq) - \tau(\ol yp) - \tau(\ol zq) + \tau(\ol zp) \end{equation} is bounded from above by all of the following values: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item $2 \min(\ol qp\, \ol yz) \tau^\prime\brOf{\max(\ol qp\, \ol yz)}$, \item $2 \,\ol qp^\beta \ol yz^{1-\beta} \tau^\prime\brOf{\ol qp^{1-\beta} \ol yz^\beta}$ for all $\beta\in[0,1]$, \item $2 \br{\beta\,\ol qp + (1-\beta)\ol yz} \tau^\prime\brOf{(1-\beta)\ol qp + \beta\ol yz}$ for all $\beta\in[0,1]$, \item $2 \sqrt{\ol qp\, \ol yz} \tau^\prime\brOf{\sqrt{\ol qp\, \ol yz}}$, \item $\br{\ol qp + \ol yz} \tau^\prime\brOf{\frac{\ol qp + \ol yz}2}$, \item $4\tau\brOf{\sqrt{\ol qp\, \ol yz}}$, \item $4\tau\brOf{\frac{\ol qp + \ol yz}2}$, \item $2\tau(\ol qp) + 2\tau(\ol yz)$. \end{enumerate}
assumptions: $(\mc Q, d)$ be a metric space
\begin{equation} \ol yq^2 - \ol yp^2 - \ol zq^2 + \ol zp^2 \leq 2\, \ol qp \, \ol yz \, . \end{equation}
conclusions: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item $2 \min(\ol qp\, \ol yz) \tau^\prime\brOf{\max(\ol qp\, \ol yz)}$, \item $2 \,\ol qp^\beta \ol yz^{1-\beta} \tau^\prime\brOf{\ol qp^{1-\beta} \ol yz^\beta}$ for all $\beta\in[0,1]$, \item $2 \br{\beta\,\ol qp + (1-\beta)\ol yz} \tau^\prime\brOf{(1-\beta)\ol qp + \beta\ol yz}$ for all $\beta\in[0,1]$, \item $2 \sqrt{\ol qp\, \ol yz} \tau^\prime\brOf{\sqrt{\ol qp\, \ol yz}}$, \item $\br{\ol qp + \ol yz} \tau^\prime\brOf{\frac{\ol qp + \ol yz}2}$, \item $4\tau\brOf{\sqrt{\ol qp\, \ol yz}}$, \item $4\tau\brOf{\frac{\ol qp + \ol yz}2}$, \item $2\tau(\ol qp) + 2\tau(\ol yz)$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.label: cor:rhsbound

nodes.name: Assumption (tau_2 quadruple inequality)
nodes.statement: \ol yq^2 - \ol yp^2 - \ol zq^2 + \ol zp^2 \leq 2\, \ol qp \, \ol yz \, .

nodes.name: Quadruple left-hand side
nodes.statement: \tau(\ol yq) - \tau(\ol yp) - \tau(\ol zq) + \tau(\ol zp)

nodes.name: Proof of Bounds for the right-hand side
nodes.statement: We first apply \cref{thm:main} twice, to $(y,z,q,p)$ and to $(q,p,y,z)$, to obtain \begin{equation} \tau(\ol yq) - \tau(\ol yp) - \tau(\ol zq) + \tau(\ol zp) \leq 2 \min(\ol qp\, \ol yz) \tau^\prime\brOf{\max(\ol qp\, \ol yz)} \, . \end{equation} This shows \ref{cor:rhsbound:min}. Let $a,b\in[0, \infty)$ and $\beta\in [0,1]$. Next we use \cref{lmm:tranconcave} \ref{lmm:tranconcave:factor} and the weighted arithmetic--geometric mean inequality, \begin{align*} \min(a,b) \tau^\prime(\max(a,b)) &\leq a^\beta b^{1-\beta} \tau^\prime(a^{1-\beta} b^\beta) \\&\leq \br{\beta a + (1-\beta)b} \tau^\prime((1-\beta)a + \beta b) \, . \end{align*} Applying these inequalities to \eqref{eq:cor:rhsbound:min} shows \ref{cor:rhsbound:geo} and \ref{cor:rhsbound:ari}, and their special cases \ref{cor:rhsbound:sqrt} and \ref{cor:rhsbound:avg}, where $\beta=1/2$. By \cref{lmm:ccdiff} \ref{lmm:ccdiff:tight} with $y=0$, we have \begin{equation} x\tau^\prime(x) \leq 2 \tau(x) \end{equation} for all $x\in[0, \infty)$. Thus, \begin{align*} \min(a,b) \tau^\prime(\max(a,b)) &\leq \sqrt{a b} \,\tau^\prime(\sqrt{a b}) \\&\leq 2\tau(\sqrt{a b}) \, , \end{align*} which yields \ref{cor:rhsbound:tran}. The remaining parts \ref{cor:rhsbound:sum} and \ref{cor:rhsbound:transum}, can be obtained using \eqref{eq:xdtrantran} and Jensen's inequality: \begin{align*} \min(a,b) \tau^\prime(\max(a,b)) &\leq \frac{a+b}2 \tau^\prime\brOf{\frac{a+b}2} \\&\leq 2\tau\brOf{\frac{a+b}2} \\&\leq \tau(a) + \tau(b) \, . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Apply Theorem 1 twice, then chain AM-GM, x tau'(x) <= 2 tau(x) and Jensen's inequality.

nodes.name: Apply Theorem 1 with both diagonal orders: part (i)
nodes.statement: We first apply \cref{thm:main} twice, to $(y,z,q,p)$ and to $(q,p,y,z)$, to obtain \begin{equation} \tau(\ol yq) - \tau(\ol yp) - \tau(\ol zq) + \tau(\ol zp) \leq 2 \min(\ol qp\, \ol yz) \tau^\prime\brOf{\max(\ol qp\, \ol yz)} \, . \end{equation} This shows \ref{cor:rhsbound:min}.
nodes.statement_short: Apply Theorem 1 with both diagonal orders: part (i)

nodes.name: Bound with min and max of diagonals
nodes.statement: \tau(\ol yq) - \tau(\ol yp) - \tau(\ol zq) + \tau(\ol zp) \leq 2 \min(\ol qp\, \ol yz) \tau^\prime\brOf{\max(\ol qp\, \ol yz)} \, .
nodes.label: eq:cor:rhsbound:min

nodes.name: Lemma 22 (ii) and weighted AM-GM bound min(a,b) tau'(max(a,b))
nodes.statement: Let $a,b\in[0, \infty)$ and $\beta\in [0,1]$. Next we use \cref{lmm:tranconcave} \ref{lmm:tranconcave:factor} and the weighted arithmetic--geometric mean inequality, \begin{align*} \min(a,b) \tau^\prime(\max(a,b)) &\leq a^\beta b^{1-\beta} \tau^\prime(a^{1-\beta} b^\beta) \\&\leq \br{\beta a + (1-\beta)b} \tau^\prime((1-\beta)a + \beta b) \, . \end{align*}

nodes.name: This gives parts (ii)-(v)
nodes.statement: Applying these inequalities to \eqref{eq:cor:rhsbound:min} shows \ref{cor:rhsbound:geo} and \ref{cor:rhsbound:ari}, and their special cases \ref{cor:rhsbound:sqrt} and \ref{cor:rhsbound:avg}, where $\beta=1/2$.
nodes.statement_short: This gives parts (ii)-(v)

nodes.name: x tau'(x) <= 2 tau(x) yields part (vi)
nodes.statement: By \cref{lmm:ccdiff} \ref{lmm:ccdiff:tight} with $y=0$, we have \begin{equation} x\tau^\prime(x) \leq 2 \tau(x) \end{equation} for all $x\in[0, \infty)$. Thus, \begin{align*} \min(a,b) \tau^\prime(\max(a,b)) &\leq \sqrt{a b} \,\tau^\prime(\sqrt{a b}) \\&\leq 2\tau(\sqrt{a b}) \, , \end{align*} which yields \ref{cor:rhsbound:tran}.
nodes.statement_short: x tau'(x) <= 2 tau(x) yields part (vi)

nodes.name: x tau'(x) <= 2 tau(x)
nodes.statement: x\tau^\prime(x) \leq 2 \tau(x)
nodes.label: eq:xdtrantran

nodes.name: Jensen's inequality yields parts (vii) and (viii)
nodes.statement: The remaining parts \ref{cor:rhsbound:sum} and \ref{cor:rhsbound:transum}, can be obtained using \eqref{eq:xdtrantran} and Jensen's inequality: \begin{align*} \min(a,b) \tau^\prime(\max(a,b)) &\leq \frac{a+b}2 \tau^\prime\brOf{\frac{a+b}2} \\&\leq 2\tau\brOf{\frac{a+b}2} \\&\leq \tau(a) + \tau(b) \, . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Jensen's inequality yields parts (vii) and (viii)

nodes.name: For three points
nodes.statement: Let $(\mc Q, d)$ be a metric space. Let $y, q, p \in \mc Q$. \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item Let $\tau\in\mc S_0$. Then \begin{equation} \tau(\ol yq) - \tau(\ol yp) + \tau(\ol qp) \leq 2 \, \ol qp \, \tau^\prime(\ol yq) \, . \end{equation} \item Let $\alpha\in[1,2]$. Then \begin{equation} \ol yq^\alpha - \ol yp^\alpha + \ol qp^\alpha \leq \alpha 2^{2-\alpha} \, \ol qp \, \ol yq^{\alpha-1} \, . \end{equation} \end{enumerate}
assumptions: $(\mc Q, d)$ be a metric space
conclusions: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item Let $\tau\in\mc S_0$. Then \begin{equation} \tau(\ol yq) - \tau(\ol yp) + \tau(\ol qp) \leq 2 \, \ol qp \, \tau^\prime(\ol yq) \, . \end{equation} \item Let $\alpha\in[1,2]$. Then \begin{equation} \ol yq^\alpha - \ol yp^\alpha + \ol qp^\alpha \leq \alpha 2^{2-\alpha} \, \ol qp \, \ol yq^{\alpha-1} \, . \end{equation} \end{enumerate}

nodes.statement: \tau(\ol yq) - \tau(\ol yp) + \tau(\ol qp) \leq 2 \, \ol qp \, \tau^\prime(\ol yq) \, .

nodes.name: Three-point power inequality
nodes.statement: \ol yq^\alpha - \ol yp^\alpha + \ol qp^\alpha \leq \alpha 2^{2-\alpha} \, \ol qp \, \ol yq^{\alpha-1} \, .
nodes.label: cor:three:pow

nodes.name: Proof of For three points
nodes.statement: By the triangle inequality, $\abs{\ol yq - \ol qp} \leq \ol yp$. After squaring this inequality, we obtain \eqref{eq:quad2} with $z=q$, which is \begin{equation} \ol yq^2 - \ol yp^2 + \ol qp^2 \leq 2 \,\ol qp \, \ol yq \, . \end{equation} Thus, \cref{thm:main} implies \eqref{cor:three:tran} and \cref{prp:powerinequ} implies \eqref{cor:three:pow}.
nodes.statement_short: Square the triangle inequality to get (5) with z=q and apply Theorem 1 and Proposition 2.

nodes.statement: By the triangle inequality, $\abs{\ol yq - \ol qp} \leq \ol yp$. After squaring this inequality, we obtain \eqref{eq:quad2} with $z=q$, which is \begin{equation} \ol yq^2 - \ol yp^2 + \ol qp^2 \leq 2 \,\ol qp \, \ol yq \, . \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Square the triangle inequality to obtain (5) with z = q

nodes.statement: \ol yq^2 - \ol yp^2 + \ol qp^2 \leq 2 \,\ol qp \, \ol yq \, .

nodes.name: Apply Theorem 1 and Proposition 2

nodes.statement_short: Apply Theorem 1 and Proposition 2

nodes.name: On the real line
nodes.statement: Let $a,b,c\in[0, \infty)$. \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item Let $\tau\in\mc S_0$. Then \begin{align} \tau(a+b+c) - \tau(a+b) - \tau(b+c) + \tau(b) &\leq 2 c \tau^\prime(a) \\ \tau(a+b+c) - \tau(a+b) - \tau(b+c) + \tau(b) &\leq \tau(c) + \tau(a) \, . \end{align} \item Let $\alpha\in[1,2]$. Then \begin{align} (a+b+c)^\alpha - (a+b)^\alpha - (b+c)^\alpha + b^\alpha &\leq \alpha 2^{2-\alpha} c a^{\alpha-1} \\ (a+b+c)^\alpha - (a+b)^\alpha - (b+c)^\alpha + b^\alpha &\leq c^\alpha + a^\alpha \, . \end{align} \end{enumerate}
conclusions: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item Let $\tau\in\mc S_0$. Then \begin{align} \tau(a+b+c) - \tau(a+b) - \tau(b+c) + \tau(b) &\leq 2 c \tau^\prime(a) \\ \tau(a+b+c) - \tau(a+b) - \tau(b+c) + \tau(b) &\leq \tau(c) + \tau(a) \, . \end{align} \item Let $\alpha\in[1,2]$. Then \begin{align} (a+b+c)^\alpha - (a+b)^\alpha - (b+c)^\alpha + b^\alpha &\leq \alpha 2^{2-\alpha} c a^{\alpha-1} \\ (a+b+c)^\alpha - (a+b)^\alpha - (b+c)^\alpha + b^\alpha &\leq c^\alpha + a^\alpha \, . \end{align} \end{enumerate}

nodes.name: Real-line quadruple inequality
nodes.statement: \tau(a+b+c) - \tau(a+b) - \tau(b+c) + \tau(b) &\leq 2 c \tau^\prime(a)
nodes.label: eq:real:quad

nodes.name: Real-line symmetric inequality
nodes.statement: \tau(a+b+c) - \tau(a+b) - \tau(b+c) + \tau(b) &\leq \tau(c) + \tau(a) \, .
nodes.label: eq:real:symm

nodes.name: Real-line power inequality
nodes.statement: (a+b+c)^\alpha - (a+b)^\alpha - (b+c)^\alpha + b^\alpha &\leq \alpha 2^{2-\alpha} c a^{\alpha-1}
nodes.label: eq:real:pow

nodes.name: Real-line symmetric power inequality
nodes.statement: (a+b+c)^\alpha - (a+b)^\alpha - (b+c)^\alpha + b^\alpha &\leq c^\alpha + a^\alpha \, .
nodes.label: eq:real:powsymm

nodes.name: Proof of On the real line
nodes.statement: In $(\mathbb{R}, \abs{\cdot - \cdot})$, \eqref{eq:quad2} is fulfilled. Choose $y = 0$, $z = a$, $p = a+b$, $q=a+b+c$ and apply \cref{thm:main} and \cref{prp:powerinequ} to obtain \eqref{eq:real:quad}. For \eqref{eq:real:symm}, apply \cref{thm:ipsymm}. To get \eqref{eq:real:pow}, use \cref{prp:powerinequ}. The equation \eqref{eq:real:powsymm} is \eqref{eq:real:symm} with $\tau = \tau_\alpha = (x\mapsto x^\alpha)$.

nodes.name: Set A of admissible distance vectors
nodes.statement: Let $A \subseteq (0, \infty)^6$ be the set of points $x = (x_1, \dots, x_6)$ such that there is a metric space $(\{y_x,z_x,q_x,p_x\}, d)$ with \begin{equation} x_1 = \ol {y_x}{q_x} \, ,\quad x_2 = \ol {y_x}{p_x} \, ,\quad x_3 = \ol {z_x}{q_x} \, ,\quad x_4 = \ol {z_x}{p_x} \, ,\quad x_5 = \ol {q_x}{p_x} \, ,\quad x_6 = \ol {y_x}{z_x} \end{equation} that fulfills \eqref{eq:quad2}.

nodes.name: Coordinates of the six distances
nodes.statement: x_1 = \ol {y_x}{q_x} \, ,\quad x_2 = \ol {y_x}{p_x} \, ,\quad x_3 = \ol {z_x}{q_x} \, ,\quad x_4 = \ol {z_x}{p_x} \, ,\quad x_5 = \ol {q_x}{p_x} \, ,\quad x_6 = \ol {y_x}{z_x}

nodes.name: Quadruple constants L_alpha, K_alpha, J_alpha
nodes.statement: For $\alpha\in(0, \infty)$, define \begin{align*} L_\alpha &:= \sup_{x\in A} \frac{\ol {y_x}{q_x}^\alpha - \ol {y_x}{p_x}^\alpha - \ol {z_x}{q_x}^\alpha + \ol {z_x}{p_x}^\alpha}{\ol {q_x}{p_x} \,\ol {y_x}{z_x}^{\alpha-1}}\, ,\\ K_\alpha &:= \sup_{x\in A} \frac{\ol {y_x}{q_x}^\alpha - \ol {y_x}{p_x}^\alpha - \ol {z_x}{q_x}^\alpha + \ol {z_x}{p_x}^\alpha}{\ol {q_x}{p_x}^{\frac\alpha2} \,\ol {y_x}{z_x}^{\frac\alpha2}}\, ,\\ J_\alpha &:= \sup_{x\in A} \frac{\ol {y_x}{q_x}^\alpha - \ol {y_x}{p_x}^\alpha - \ol {z_x}{q_x}^\alpha + \ol {z_x}{p_x}^\alpha}{\ol {q_x}{p_x}^\alpha + \ol {y_x}{z_x}^\alpha}\, . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Sharp constants of the power quadruple inequality with asymmetric, geometric-mean and sum right-hand sides.

nodes.name: Quadruple constants L_S0, K_S0, J_S0
nodes.statement: Furthermore, define \begin{align*} L_{\mc S_0} &:= \sup_{\tau\in\mc S_0} \sup_{x\in A} \frac{\tau(\ol {y_x}{q_x}) - \tau(\ol {y_x}{p_x}) - \tau(\ol {z_x}{q_x}) + \tau(\ol {z_x}{p_x})}{\ol {q_x}{p_x} \,\tau^\prime(\ol {y_x}{z_x})}\, ,\\ K_{\mc S_0} &:= \sup_{\tau\in\mc S_0} \sup_{x\in A} \frac{\tau(\ol {y_x}{q_x}) - \tau(\ol {y_x}{p_x}) - \tau(\ol {z_x}{q_x}) + \tau(\ol {z_x}{p_x})}{\tau(\sqrt{\ol {q_x}{p_x}\,\ol {y_x}{z_x}})}\, ,\\ J_{\mc S_0} &:= \sup_{\tau\in\mc S_0} \sup_{x\in A} \frac{\tau(\ol {y_x}{q_x}) - \tau(\ol {y_x}{p_x}) - \tau(\ol {z_x}{q_x}) + \tau(\ol {z_x}{p_x})}{\tau(\ol {q_x}{p_x}) + \tau(\ol {y_x}{z_x})}\, . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: The same three sharp constants with a supremum over tau in S_0.

nodes.name: Summary of quadruple constants
nodes.statement: \mbox{ } \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item $L_\alpha = \alpha 2^{2-\alpha}$ for $\alpha\in[1,2]$ and $L_\alpha = \infty$ for $\alpha\in(0, \infty)\setminus[1,2]$. \item $K_\alpha = 2$ for $\alpha\in(0,1]$, $K_\alpha \in [2, \alpha 2^{2-\alpha}]$ for $\alpha\in[1,2]$, $K_\alpha = \infty$ for $\alpha\in(2,\infty)$. \item $J_\alpha = 1$ for $\alpha\in(0,1]$, $J_\alpha \in [1, \alpha 2^{1-\alpha}]$ for $\alpha\in[1,2]$, $J_\alpha = \infty$ for $\alpha\in(2,\infty)$. \item $L_{\mc S_0} = 2$. \item $K_{\mc S_0} \in [2, 4]$. \item $J_{\mc S_0} \in [1, 2]$. \end{enumerate}
conclusions: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item $L_\alpha = \alpha 2^{2-\alpha}$ for $\alpha\in[1,2]$ and $L_\alpha = \infty$ for $\alpha\in(0, \infty)\setminus[1,2]$. \item $K_\alpha = 2$ for $\alpha\in(0,1]$, $K_\alpha \in [2, \alpha 2^{2-\alpha}]$ for $\alpha\in[1,2]$, $K_\alpha = \infty$ for $\alpha\in(2,\infty)$. \item $J_\alpha = 1$ for $\alpha\in(0,1]$, $J_\alpha \in [1, \alpha 2^{1-\alpha}]$ for $\alpha\in[1,2]$, $J_\alpha = \infty$ for $\alpha\in(2,\infty)$. \item $L_{\mc S_0} = 2$. \item $K_{\mc S_0} \in [2, 4]$. \item $J_{\mc S_0} \in [1, 2]$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.label: prp:summary

nodes.name: Proof of Summary of quadruple constants
nodes.statement: From \cref{prp:powerinequ}, we know $L_\alpha = \alpha 2^{2-\alpha}$ for $\alpha\in[1,2]$ and $L_\alpha = \infty$ for $\alpha\in(0, \infty)\setminus[1,2]$. As direct consequences, we obtain $K_\alpha \leq \alpha 2^{2-\alpha}$ and $J_\alpha \leq \alpha 2^{1-\alpha}$ for $\alpha\in[1,2]$. If we set $y = p$ and $z = q$ and assume $\ol yq = a \in (0, \infty)$, we have \begin{align*} \tau(\ol yq) - \tau(\ol yp) - \tau(\ol zq) + \tau(\ol zp) &= 2 \tau(a)\, ,\\ \tau(\sqrt{\ol {q}{p}\,\ol {y}{z}}) &= \tau(a) \, ,\\ \tau(\ol {q}{p}) + \tau(\ol {y}{z}) &= 2\tau(a) \, , \end{align*} for any function $\tau\colon(0, \infty)\to\mathbb{R}$ with $\tau(0) = 0$. Thus, $K_\alpha, K_{\mc S_0} \geq 2$, $J_\alpha, J_{\mc S_0} \geq 1$. If $\tau$ is metric preserving, like $\tau_\alpha = (x\mapsto x^\alpha)$ with $\alpha\in(0,1]$, then \begin{equation} \tau(\ol yq) - \tau(\ol yp) - \tau(\ol zq) + \tau(\ol zp) \leq 2\min\brOf{\tau(\ol qp), \tau(\ol yz)} \, . \end{equation} This shows $K_\alpha \leq 2$ and $J_\alpha \leq 1$ for $\alpha\in(0,1]$. Let $y = (0,0)$, $z = (0,\epsilon)$, $q = (1,\epsilon)$, $p = (1, 0)$ in the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$, see \cref{fig:quadriRect}. Then \begin{align*} \tau(\ol yq) - \tau(\ol yp) - \tau(\ol zq) + \tau(\ol zp) &= 2 \tau(\sqrt{\epsilon^2+1}) - 2 \tau(1)\, ,\\ \tau(\sqrt{\ol {q}{p}\,\ol {y}{z}}) &= \tau(\epsilon) \, ,\\ \tau(\ol {q}{p}) + \tau(\ol {y}{z}) &= 2\tau(\epsilon) \, , \end{align*} for any function $\tau\colon[0, \infty)\to\mathbb{R}$. Assume $\tau(0) = 0$, $\tau^\prime(1) > 0$, and $\lim_{\epsilon\searrow0} \frac{\epsilon}{\tau^\prime(\epsilon)} = \infty$. Then, by l'Hôpital's rule, \begin{equation} \lim_{\epsilon\searrow0} \frac{\tau(\sqrt{\epsilon^2+1}) - \tau(1)}{\tau(\epsilon)} = \lim_{\epsilon\searrow0} \frac{\epsilon \tau^\prime(\sqrt{\epsilon^2+1})}{\sqrt{\epsilon^2+1}\,\tau^\prime(\epsilon)} = \infty\, . \end{equation} In particular, $K_\alpha = \infty$ and $J_\alpha = \infty$ for $\alpha\in(2,\infty)$. By \cref{thm:main} and \cref{cor:rhsbound}, we have $L_{\mc S_0} \leq 2$, $K_{\mc S_0} \leq 4$, and $J_{\mc S_0} \leq 2$. As here we take the supremum over $\tau\in\mc S_0$, we also get $L_{\mc S_0} \geq 2$, e.g., for $\tau = \tau_1 = (x\mapsto x)$.
nodes.statement_short: Combine Proposition 2, degenerate and thin-rectangle configurations, and Theorem 1 with Corollary 1.

nodes.name: Density convention for the appendix
nodes.statement: If we want to show $f(x)\leq0$ for all $x\in A$, where $A\subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$, for a continuous function $f\colon A\to \mathbb{R}$, it is enough to prove the inequality on a dense subset of $A$. We use this fact in the following. If we write an expression with a quotient, we silently restrict the domains of the real parameters in all statements about this expression to a domain on which the denominator is not 0. The restricted domain, will always be dense in the unrestricted domain.
nodes.statement_short: Inequalities of continuous functions need only be shown on dense subsets; quotients silently restrict to dense domains.

nodes.name: Properties of tau_sqrt
nodes.statement: Let $\tau\in\mc S_0$. \begin{itemize} \item Then $\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}$ is nonnegative, nondecreasing, and concave. \item If $\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}$ is differentiable, then $\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime$ is nonnegative and nonincreasing. \item If $\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}$ is twice differentiable, then $\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^{\prime\prime}$ is nonpositive. \end{itemize}
conclusions: \label{lmm:ccsqrtprop} Let $\tau\in\mc S_0$. \begin{itemize} \item Then $\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}$ is nonnegative, nondecreasing, and concave. \item If $\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}$ is differentiable, then $\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime$ is nonnegative and nonincreasing. \item If $\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}$ is twice differentiable, then $\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^{\prime\prime}$ is nonpositive. \end{itemize}
nodes.label: lmm:ccsqrtprop

nodes.name: Proof of Properties of tau_sqrt
nodes.statement: As $\tau$ is nonnegative, so is $\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}$. We have \begin{align*} \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime(x) &= \frac{\tau^\prime(\sqrt{x})}{2 \sqrt{x}}\, ,\\ \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^{\prime\prime}(x) &= \frac{\tau^{\prime\prime}(\sqrt{x})-\frac{\tau^\prime(\sqrt{x})}{\sqrt{x}}}{4x}\, . \end{align*} As $\tau^\prime$ is nonnegative, so is $\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime$. Thus, $\tau$ is increasing. Furthermore, as $\tau^{\prime\prime}$ is nonincreasing, \begin{equation} \tau^\prime(\sqrt{x}) - \tau^\prime(0) = \int_0^{\sqrt{x}} \tau^{\prime\prime}(u) \mathrm{d} u \geq \sqrt{x} \tau^{\prime\prime}(x) \, . \end{equation} Thus, with $\tau^\prime(0) \geq 0$, we obtain $\tau^\prime(\sqrt{x}) \geq \sqrt{x} \tau^{\prime\prime}(x)$. Hence, $\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^{\prime\prime}$ is nonpositive, $\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime$ is nonincreasing, and $\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}$ is concave.
nodes.statement_short: Differentiate tau(sqrt x) and use the sign and monotonicity properties of tau', tau''.

nodes.name: Nonnegativity and monotonicity from the derivative formulas of tau_sqrt
nodes.statement: As $\tau$ is nonnegative, so is $\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}$. We have \begin{align*} \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime(x) &= \frac{\tau^\prime(\sqrt{x})}{2 \sqrt{x}}\, ,\\ \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^{\prime\prime}(x) &= \frac{\tau^{\prime\prime}(\sqrt{x})-\frac{\tau^\prime(\sqrt{x})}{\sqrt{x}}}{4x}\, . \end{align*} As $\tau^\prime$ is nonnegative, so is $\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime$. Thus, $\tau$ is increasing.
nodes.statement_short: Nonnegativity and monotonicity from the derivative formulas of tau_sqrt

nodes.name: Shorthand notation for monotonicity and curvature
nodes.statement: There and in the proof below, we use following shorthand notation for properties of functions $f \colon [0, \infty) \to \mathbb{R}$: \vspace{\topsep+\parskip} \noindent\begin{minipage}{0.49\textwidth} \begin{itemize} \item $f \geq0$: $f$ is nonnegative. \item $f \nearrow$: $f$ is nondecreasing. \item $f \smallsmile$: $f$ is convex. \end{itemize} \end{minipage} \begin{minipage}{0.49\textwidth} \begin{itemize} \item $f \leq0$: $f$ is nonpositive. \item $f \searrow$: $f$ is nonincreasing. \item $f \smallfrown$: $f$ is concave. \end{itemize} \end{minipage}

nodes.name: Elimination of r
nodes.statement: Let $\tau\in\setccod3$. \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item For all $a,b,c\in[0, \infty)$, $s\in [-1, \min(1, 2\frac ac -1)]$, we have \begin{equation} \tau(a) - \tau(c) -\tau(\abs{a-b}) + \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(c^2 - 2scb + b^2) \leq 2b \tau^\prime(a-sc)\ \, . \end{equation} \item For all $a,b,c\in[0, \infty)$ with $a\geq c$, we have \begin{equation} \tau(a) - \tau(c) -\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}((a-b)^2 - 4bc) + \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(b + c) \leq 2b \tau^\prime(a-c) \, . \end{equation} \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Two one-parameter-free inequalities (r eliminated) that imply Theorem 3.
conclusions: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item For all $a,b,c\in[0, \infty)$, $s\in [-1, \min(1, 2\frac ac -1)]$, we have \begin{equation} \tau(a) - \tau(c) -\tau(\abs{a-b}) + \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(c^2 - 2scb + b^2) \leq 2b \tau^\prime(a-sc)\ \, . \end{equation} \item For all $a,b,c\in[0, \infty)$ with $a\geq c$, we have \begin{equation} \tau(a) - \tau(c) -\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}((a-b)^2 - 4bc) + \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(b + c) \leq 2b \tau^\prime(a-c) \, . \end{equation} \end{enumerate}

nodes.name: Case conditions on r and s
nodes.statement: Let $a,b,c\geq0$, $r,s\in[-1,1]$. Then \begin{align*} &ra - sc \geq a-c \quad\Leftrightarrow\quad s \leq (r-1) \frac ac+1 \quad\Leftrightarrow\quad r \geq (s-1)\frac ca +1 \, , \\ &ra - sc \geq c-a \quad\Leftrightarrow\quad s \leq (r+1) \frac ac -1 \quad\Leftrightarrow\quad r \geq (s+1)\frac ca -1 \, . \end{align*}
conclusions: \begin{align*} &ra - sc \geq a-c \quad\Leftrightarrow\quad s \leq (r-1) \frac ac+1 \quad\Leftrightarrow\quad r \geq (s-1)\frac ca +1 \, , \\ &ra - sc \geq c-a \quad\Leftrightarrow\quad s \leq (r+1) \frac ac -1 \quad\Leftrightarrow\quad r \geq (s+1)\frac ca -1 \, . \end{align*}

nodes.name: Functions ell_tau and F_tau
nodes.statement: Denote \begin{align*} \ell_{\tau}(a,b,c,r,s) &:= \tau(a) - \tau(c) - \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}\brOf{a^2-2rab+b^2} + \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}\brOf{c^2-2scb+b^2}\, ,\\ F_{\tau}(a,b,c,r,s) &:= \ell_{\tau}(a,b,c,r,s) - 2 b \tau^\prime\brOf{ra - sc} \, . \end{align*}

nodes.name: Convexity in r
nodes.statement: Let $\tau\in\setccod3$. Let $a,b,c\geq0$, $s,r\in[-1,1]$. Assume $ra - sc \geq 0$. Then \begin{equation*} \partial_r^2 F_{\tau}(a,b,c,r,s) \geq 0 \, . \end{equation*}
conclusions: \begin{equation*} \partial_r^2 F_{\tau}(a,b,c,r,s) \geq 0 \, . \end{equation*}
nodes.label: lmm:ddr

nodes.name: Proof of Convexity in r
nodes.statement: As $\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^{\prime\prime},\tau^{\prime\prime\prime}\leq0$, we have \begin{align*} \partial_r^2 \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}\brOf{a^2-2rab+b^2} = 4a^2b^2\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^{\prime\prime}(a^2-2rab+b^2) \leq 0\, , \partial_r^2 \tau^\prime(ra - sc) = a^2 \tau^{\prime\prime\prime}(ra - sc) \leq 0 \, . \end{align*} Thus, \begin{equation*} \partial_r^2 F_{\tau}(a,b,c,r,s) = -\partial_r^2 \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}\brOf{a^2-2rab+b^2} - 2 b \partial_r^2\tau^\prime\brOf{ra - sc} \geq 0 \, . \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Second derivative in r of F is nonnegative because tau_sqrt'' <= 0 and tau''' <= 0.

nodes.name: Maximizing the left-hand side for |a-c| >= ra-sc
nodes.statement: Let $\tau\in\setccod3$. Let $a,b,c\in[0, \infty)$, $r,s\in[-1, 1]$. Assume $|a-c| \geq ra-sc$. \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item If $a\geq c$ and $a^2 \leq c^2+2ab-2cb$, then \begin{equation*} \ell_{\tau}(a,b,c,r,s) \leq \tau(a)-\tau(c)-\tau(|a-b|)+\tau(|c-b|) \, . \end{equation*} \item If $a\geq c$ and $a^2 \geq c^2+2ab-2cb$, then \begin{equation*} \ell_{\tau}(a,b,c,r,s) \leq \tau(a)-\tau(c)-\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}((a-b)^2+4cb)+\tau(c+b) \, . \end{equation*} \item If $a\leq c$, then \begin{equation*} \ell_{\tau}(a,b,c,r,s) \leq \tau(a)-\tau(c)-\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(\abs{a-b})+\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}((c+b)^2-4ab) \, . \end{equation*} \end{enumerate}
conclusions: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item If $a\geq c$ and $a^2 \leq c^2+2ab-2cb$, then \begin{equation*} \ell_{\tau}(a,b,c,r,s) \leq \tau(a)-\tau(c)-\tau(|a-b|)+\tau(|c-b|) \, . \end{equation*} \item If $a\geq c$ and $a^2 \geq c^2+2ab-2cb$, then \begin{equation*} \ell_{\tau}(a,b,c,r,s) \leq \tau(a)-\tau(c)-\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}((a-b)^2+4cb)+\tau(c+b) \, . \end{equation*} \item If $a\leq c$, then \begin{equation*} \ell_{\tau}(a,b,c,r,s) \leq \tau(a)-\tau(c)-\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(\abs{a-b})+\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}((c+b)^2-4ab) \, . \end{equation*} \end{enumerate}
nodes.label: lmm:maxlhs

nodes.name: Proof of Maximizing the left-hand side for |a-c| >= ra-sc
nodes.statement: As $\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}\nearrow$, $s\mapsto\ell_{\tau}(a,b,c,r,s) \searrow$ and $r\mapsto\ell_{\tau}(a,b,c,r,s) \nearrow$, i.e., for $s_0,r_0\in[-1,1]$, \begin{equation*} \max_{s\geq s_0, r\leq r_0} \ell_{\tau}(a,b,c,r,s) = \ell_{\tau}(a,b,c,r_0,s_0) \, . \end{equation*} \underline{Case 1: $a\geq c$.} For $r\in[-1,1]$, set $s_{\ms{min}}(r) := (r-1) \frac ac+1$, cf.\ \cref{lmm:srbound}. Define \begin{align*} f(r) &:= \ell_{\tau}(a,b,c,r,s_{\ms{min}}(r)) \\&= \tau(a)-\tau(c)-\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(a^2-2rab+b^2)+\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(c^2-2rab+2ab-2cb+b^2) \, . \end{align*} Then \begin{equation*} \frac{f^\prime(r)}{2ab} = \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime(a^2-2rab+b^2) - \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime(c^2-2rab+2ab-2cb+b^2) \, . \end{equation*} \underline{Case 1.1: $a^2 \leq c^2+2ab-2cb$.} As $\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime\searrow$, we have \begin{align*} a^2-2rab+b^2 &\leq c^2-2rab+2ab-2cb+b^2\, ,\\ \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime(a^2-2rab+b^2) &\geq \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime(c^2-2rab+2ab-2cb+b^2) \, . \end{align*} Thus, $f^\prime(r)\geq0$ and $f$ is maximal at $r = r_{\ms{max}} = 1$, with $s_{\ms{min}}(r) = 1$. Hence, \begin{equation*} \ell_{\tau}(a,b,c,r,s) \leq f(1) = \tau(a)-\tau(c)-\tau(|a-b|)+\tau(|c-b|) \, . \end{equation*} \underline{Case 1.2: $a^2 \geq c^2+2ab-2cb$.} As $\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime\searrow$, we have \begin{align*} a^2-2rab+b^2 &\geq c^2-2rab+2ab-2cb+b^2\, ,\\ \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime(a^2-2rab+b^2) &\leq \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime(c^2-2rab+2ab-2cb+b^2) \, . \end{align*} Thus, $f^\prime(r)\leq0$ and $f$ is maximal at $r = r_{\ms{min}} = 1-2\frac ca$, with $s_{\ms{min}}(r) = -1$. Hence, \begin{equation*} \ell_{\tau}(a,b,c,r,s) \leq f(r_{\ms{min}}) = \tau(a)-\tau(c)-\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}((a-b)^2+4cb)+\tau(c+b) \, . \end{equation*} \underline{Case 2: $a\leq c$.} For $r\in[-1,1]$, set $s_{\ms{min}}(r) := (r+1) \frac ac-1$, cf.\ \cref{lmm:srbound}. Define \begin{align*} f(r) &:= \ell_{\tau}(a,b,c,r,s_{\ms{min}}(r)) \\&= \tau(a)-\tau(c)-\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(a^2-2rab+b^2)+\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(c^2-2rab-2ab+2cb+b^2) \, . \end{align*} Then \begin{equation*} \frac{f^\prime(r)}{2ab} = \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime(a^2-2rab+b^2) - \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime(c^2-2rab-2ab+2cb+b^2) \, . \end{equation*} \underline{Case 2.1: $a^2 \leq c^2-2ab+2cb$.} As $\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime\searrow$, we have \begin{align*} a^2-2rab+b^2 &\leq c^2-2rab-2ab+2cb+b^2\, ,\\ \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime(a^2-2rab+b^2) &\geq \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime(c^2-2rab-2ab+2cb+b^2)\, . \end{align*} Thus, $f^\prime(r)\geq0$ and $f$ is maximal at $r = r_{\ms{max}} = 1$, with $s_{\ms{min}}(r) = 2\frac ac-1$. Hence, \begin{equation*} \ell_{\tau}(a,b,c,r,s) \leq f(1) = \tau(a)-\tau(c)-\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(\abs{a-b})+\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}((c+b)^2-4ab) \, . \end{equation*} \underline{Case 2.2: $a^2 \geq c^2-2ab+2cb$.} This cannot happen for $a < c$. Hence, the proof is finished.
nodes.statement_short: Case analysis on a >= c vs a <= c; restrict s to its boundary and maximize f(r) via the sign of f'.

nodes.name: Proof of Parametrized quadruple inequality
nodes.statement: \mbox{ }\\ \underline{Case 1: $|a-c| \geq ra-sc$.}\\ \underline{Case 1.1: $a\geq c$.} We can apply \cref{lmm:maxlhs} and it suffices to show \begin{equation} \tau(a)-\tau(c)-\tau(|a-b|)+\tau(|c-b|) \leq 2 b \tau^\prime(a - c) \end{equation} for $a^2 \leq c^2+2ab-2cb$, and for $a^2 \geq c^2+2ab-2cb$, \begin{equation} \tau(a)-\tau(c)-\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}((a-b)^2+4cb)+\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(c+b) \leq 2 b \tau^\prime(a - c) \, . \end{equation} The latter is exactly \cref{lmm:param:firstreduction} \ref{lmm:param:firstreduction:b}. The former follows from \cref{lmm:param:firstreduction} \ref{lmm:param:firstreduction:a} with $s\in\{-1, 1\}$. \\ \underline{Case 1.2: $a\leq c$.} We can apply \cref{lmm:maxlhs} and it suffices to show \begin{equation} \tau(a)-\tau(c)-\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(\abs{a-b})+\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}((c+b)^2-4ab) \leq 2 b \tau^\prime(c - a) \, . \end{equation} This follows from \cref{lmm:param:firstreduction} \ref{lmm:param:firstreduction:a} with $s = 2\frac ac-1$. \\ \underline{Case 2: $|a-c| \leq ra-sc$.}\\ \underline{Case 2.1: $a\geq c$.} In this case, $F_{\tau}(a,b,c,r,s) \leq 0$ implies \eqref{eq:thm:main:param}. As $r\mapsto F_{\tau}(a,b,c,r,s)$ is convex by \cref{lmm:ddr}, it suffices to show $F_{\tau}(a,b,c,r,s) \leq 0$ for the extreme values of $r$ in order to establish this inequality for all $r$. By \cref{lmm:srbound}, \begin{equation} r\in\abOf{(s-1)\frac ca+1,\, 1}\, . \end{equation} For maximal $r$, by \cref{lmm:param:firstreduction} \ref{lmm:param:firstreduction:a}, we have $F_{\tau}(a,b,c,1,s) \leq 0$. For minimal $r$, we have $ra-sc = a-c$. Thus, we are in case 1.1. \\ \underline{Case 2.2: $a\leq c$.} As in case 2.1, it suffices show $F_{\tau}(a,b,c,r,s) \leq 0$ for extreme values of $r$. By \cref{lmm:srbound}, \begin{equation} r\in\abOf{(s+1)\frac ca -1,\, 1} \, . \end{equation} For maximal $r$, by \cref{lmm:param:firstreduction} \ref{lmm:param:firstreduction:a}, we have $F_{\tau}(a,b,c,1,s) \leq 0$. For minimal $r$, we have $ra-sc = c-a$. Thus, we are in case 1.2.
nodes.statement_short: Case analysis on |a-c| vs ra-sc and a vs c, reducing to Lemma 9 via Lemma 12 and convexity in r (Lemma 11).
