nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 9 (i) for c >= a >= b >= sc
nodes.statement: Define \begin{align*} f(a,b,c,s) &:= \tau(a)-\tau(c)-\tau(a-b)+\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(c^2-2scb+b^2) - 2 b \tau^\prime(a - sc)\, ,\\ \partial_b f(a,b,c,s) &= \tau^\prime(a-b) + 2(b-sc)\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime(c^2-2scb+b^2) - 2 \tau^\prime(a - sc) \, . \end{align*} By \cref{mech:3}, $\partial_b f(a,b,c,s) \leq 0$. Thus, as $b \geq b_{\ms{min}} := \max(0, sc)$, we have $f(a,b,c,s) \leq f(a,b_{\ms{min}},c,s)$. If $s \leq 0$, then $b_{\ms{min}}=0$ and \begin{equation*} f(a,0,c,s) = \tau(a)-\tau(c)-\tau(a)+\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(c^2) = 0 \, . \end{equation*} For $s\geq 0$, we have $b_{\ms{min}}=sc$. Define \begin{align} g(a,c,s) &:= f(a,sc,c,s) = \tau(a)-\tau(c)-\tau(a-sc)+\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}((1-s^2)c^2) - 2 sc\tau^\prime(a - sc)\, ,\\ \partial_a g(a,c,s) &= \tau^\prime(a)-\tau^\prime(a-sc) - 2 sc\tau^{\prime\prime}(a - sc)\, . \end{align} Set $d:= sc$ and define \begin{equation} h(a, d) := \tau^\prime(a)-\tau^\prime(a-d) - 2 d\tau^{\prime\prime}(a - d) = \partial_a g(a,c,s)\, . \end{equation} Then \begin{equation} \partial_{d} h(a, d) = -\tau^{\prime\prime}(a - d) + 2 d\tau^{\prime\prime\prime}(a - d) \leq 0 \, . \end{equation} As $d = sc$ and $s,c\geq 0$, we obtain \begin{equation*} h(a, d) \leq h(a, 0) = 0 \, . \end{equation*} Thus, $\partial_a g(a,c,s) = h(a, d) \leq 0$. Therefore, as $a \geq a_{\ms{min}} := \frac{s+1}{2}c$, \begin{align*} g(a,c,s) &\leq g(a_{\ms{min}},c,s) \\&= \tau(\frac{s+1}{2}c)-\tau(c)-\tau(\frac{1-s}{2}c)+\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}((1-s^2)c^2) - 2 sc\tau^\prime(\frac{1-s}{2}c) \, . \end{align*} Set $u := \frac12(c+sc)$, $v := \frac12(c-sc)$ with $0\leq v \leq u$ due to $s \in[0,1]$, and define \begin{equation} \ell(u, v) := \tau(u)-\tau(u+v)-\tau(v)+\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(4uv) - 2 (u-v)\tau^\prime(v) = g(a_{\ms{min}},c,s) \, . \end{equation} By \cref{mech:5}, $\partial_u \ell(u, v) \leq 0$. Thus, as $u \geq v$, we have \begin{align*} \ell(u, v) &\leq \ell(v, v) \\&= \tau(v)-\tau(2v)-\tau(v)+\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(4vv) - 2(v-v)\tau^\prime(v) \\&= 0 \, . \end{align*} Therefore, we obtain $f(a,sc,c,s) \leq g(a,c,s) \leq \ell(u, v) \leq 0$ and we have finally shown $f(a,b,c,s) \leq 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Monotonicity in b, then in a, then a substitution (u,v), each shown by a sign of a partial derivative via mechanical lemmas.

nodes.label: lmm:gbcs

nodes.name: Proof of Derivative bound for g(b,c,s)
nodes.statement: We have \begin{align*} \partial_b g(b,c,s) &= \tau^\prime\brOf{\frac12(1+s)c - b} - 2(sc-b)\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime(c^2-2scb+b^2) - 2\tau^\prime\brOf{\frac12(1-s)c}\, , \\ \partial_c g(b,c,s) &= \frac12(1+s)\tau^\prime\brOf{\frac12(1+s)c} - \tau^\prime(c) - \frac12(1+s)\tau^\prime\brOf{\frac12(1+s)c - b} + \\&\hphantom{=}\ \ 2(c-sb)\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime(c^2-2scb+b^2) - (1-s)b\tau^{\prime\prime}\brOf{\frac12(1-s)c} \, . \end{align*} Define \begin{align*} f(b,c,s) &:= \frac{(1-s)c}2\tau^\prime( c-b) + 2(1-s)(b+c)\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime( (c-b)^2) - 2\tau^\prime\brOf{\frac{(1-s)c}2} + \\&\hphantom{=}\ \ -\frac{(1-s)c}2\tau^\prime( c) - b(1-s)\tau^{\prime\prime}\brOf{\frac{c-b}2} \, . \end{align*} By \cref{mech:17}, \begin{equation} \partial_b g(b,c,s) + \partial_c g(b,c,s) \leq f(b,c,s)\, . \end{equation} As $\tau^{\prime\prime\prime}\leq0$, we have \begin{equation*} \partial_s^2 f(b,c,s) = - 2 (-c/2)^2\tau^{\prime\prime\prime}\brOf{\frac{(1-s)c}2} \geq 0 \, , \end{equation*} i.e., $f(b,c,s) $ is convex in $s$. Thus, to show $f(b,c,s) \leq 0$, we only need to check the extremes of $s$, $s_{\ms{min}} := \frac bc$ and $s_{\ms{max}} := 1$. For maximal $s$, we have \begin{equation*} f(b,c,s_{\ms{max}}) = - 2\tau^\prime(0) \leq 0 \, . \end{equation*} For minimal $s$, set $u := c-b\in[0,c]$. We define \begin{align*} h(u,c) &:= c f(c-u, c, s_{\ms{min}}) \\&= \frac{4c-u}2\tau^\prime(u) - 2c\tau^\prime(u/2) - \frac u2 \tau^\prime(c) - (c-u)u\tau^{\prime\prime}(u/2) \, . \end{align*} By \cref{mech:15}, $\partial_c h(u,c) \leq 0$. Thus, as $c \geq u$, we have $h(u,c) \leq h(u,u)$. By \cref{mech:16}, $h(u,u) \leq 0$. Thus, $c f(b, c, s_{\ms{min}}) = h(u,c) \leq h(u,u) \leq 0$. Because $ f(b,c,s)$ is convex in $s$ and negative for the extremes of $s$, we obtain \begin{equation*} \partial_b g(b,c,s) + \partial_c g(b,c,s) \leq f(b,c,s) \leq 0 \, . \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Bound the derivative sum by f (mech:17), use convexity of f in s and check the extreme values of s.
nodes.section: B.5 Proof of 9 lmm:param:firstreduction:a for $c \geq a \geq b$, $b \leq sc$

nodes.name: Compute partial_b g and partial_c g
nodes.statement: We have \begin{align*} \partial_b g(b,c,s) &= \tau^\prime\brOf{\frac12(1+s)c - b} - 2(sc-b)\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime(c^2-2scb+b^2) - 2\tau^\prime\brOf{\frac12(1-s)c}\, , \\ \partial_c g(b,c,s) &= \frac12(1+s)\tau^\prime\brOf{\frac12(1+s)c} - \tau^\prime(c) - \frac12(1+s)\tau^\prime\brOf{\frac12(1+s)c - b} + \\&\hphantom{=}\ \ 2(c-sb)\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime(c^2-2scb+b^2) - (1-s)b\tau^{\prime\prime}\brOf{\frac12(1-s)c} \, . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Compute partial_b g and partial_c g
nodes.section: B.5 Proof of 9 lmm:param:firstreduction:a for $c \geq a \geq b$, $b \leq sc$

nodes.name: Bound partial_b g + partial_c g by f(b,c,s) via mech:17
nodes.statement: Define \begin{align*} f(b,c,s) &:= \frac{(1-s)c}2\tau^\prime( c-b) + 2(1-s)(b+c)\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime( (c-b)^2) - 2\tau^\prime\brOf{\frac{(1-s)c}2} + \\&\hphantom{=}\ \ -\frac{(1-s)c}2\tau^\prime( c) - b(1-s)\tau^{\prime\prime}\brOf{\frac{c-b}2} \, . \end{align*} By \cref{mech:17}, \begin{equation} \partial_b g(b,c,s) + \partial_c g(b,c,s) \leq f(b,c,s)\, . \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Bound partial_b g + partial_c g by f(b,c,s) via mech:17
nodes.section: B.5 Proof of 9 lmm:param:firstreduction:a for $c \geq a \geq b$, $b \leq sc$

nodes.name: Bound of partial_b g + partial_c g by f
nodes.statement: \partial_b g(b,c,s) + \partial_c g(b,c,s) \leq f(b,c,s)\, .
nodes.section: B.5 Proof of 9 lmm:param:firstreduction:a for $c \geq a \geq b$, $b \leq sc$

nodes.name: f is convex in s, so it suffices to check s_min = b/c and s_max = 1
nodes.statement: As $\tau^{\prime\prime\prime}\leq0$, we have \begin{equation*} \partial_s^2 f(b,c,s) = - 2 (-c/2)^2\tau^{\prime\prime\prime}\brOf{\frac{(1-s)c}2} \geq 0 \, , \end{equation*} i.e., $f(b,c,s) $ is convex in $s$. Thus, to show $f(b,c,s) \leq 0$, we only need to check the extremes of $s$, $s_{\ms{min}} := \frac bc$ and $s_{\ms{max}} := 1$.
nodes.statement_short: f is convex in s, so it suffices to check s_min = b/c and s_max = 1
nodes.section: B.5 Proof of 9 lmm:param:firstreduction:a for $c \geq a \geq b$, $b \leq sc$

nodes.name: s = s_max: f = -2 tau'(0) <= 0
nodes.statement: For maximal $s$, we have \begin{equation*} f(b,c,s_{\ms{max}}) = - 2\tau^\prime(0) \leq 0 \, . \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: s = s_max: f = -2 tau'(0) <= 0
nodes.section: B.5 Proof of 9 lmm:param:firstreduction:a for $c \geq a \geq b$, $b \leq sc$

nodes.name: s = s_min: reduce to h(u,c) and apply mech:15 and mech:16
nodes.statement: For minimal $s$, set $u := c-b\in[0,c]$. We define \begin{align*} h(u,c) &:= c f(c-u, c, s_{\ms{min}}) \\&= \frac{4c-u}2\tau^\prime(u) - 2c\tau^\prime(u/2) - \frac u2 \tau^\prime(c) - (c-u)u\tau^{\prime\prime}(u/2) \, . \end{align*} By \cref{mech:15}, $\partial_c h(u,c) \leq 0$. Thus, as $c \geq u$, we have $h(u,c) \leq h(u,u)$. By \cref{mech:16}, $h(u,u) \leq 0$. Thus, $c f(b, c, s_{\ms{min}}) = h(u,c) \leq h(u,u) \leq 0$.
nodes.statement_short: s = s_min: reduce to h(u,c) and apply mech:15 and mech:16
nodes.section: B.5 Proof of 9 lmm:param:firstreduction:a for $c \geq a \geq b$, $b \leq sc$

nodes.name: Convexity in s gives partial_b g + partial_c g <= f <= 0
nodes.statement: Because $ f(b,c,s)$ is convex in $s$ and negative for the extremes of $s$, we obtain \begin{equation*} \partial_b g(b,c,s) + \partial_c g(b,c,s) \leq f(b,c,s) \leq 0 \, . \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Convexity in s gives partial_b g + partial_c g <= f <= 0
nodes.section: B.5 Proof of 9 lmm:param:firstreduction:a for $c \geq a \geq b$, $b \leq sc$

nodes.name: Lemma 9 (i) for c >= a, a <= b
nodes.statement: Let $\tau\in\setccod3$. Let $a,b,c\geq0$, $s\in[-1,1]$. Assume $(s+1)c\leq 2a$, $c \geq a$, $a \leq b$. Then \begin{equation*} \tau(a)-\tau(c)-\tau(a-b)+\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(c^2-2scb+b^2) \leq 2 b \tau^\prime(a - sc) \, . \end{equation*}
nodes.section: B.6 Proof of 9 lmm:param:firstreduction:a for $c \geq a$, $a \leq b$
conclusions: \begin{equation*} \tau(a)-\tau(c)-\tau(a-b)+\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(c^2-2scb+b^2) \leq 2 b \tau^\prime(a - sc) \, . \end{equation*}
nodes.label: lmm:param:reduicGaLb

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 9 (i) for c >= a, a <= b
nodes.statement: Define \begin{equation*} f(a,b,c,s) := \tau(a)-\tau(c)-\tau(b-a)+\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(c^2-2scb+b^2) - 2 b \tau^\prime(a - sc) \, . \end{equation*} By \cref{mech:6}, $\partial_b f(a,b,c,s)\leq0$. Thus, as $b \geq a$, we have \begin{align*} f(a,b,c,s) &\leq f(a,a,c,s) \\&= \tau(a)-\tau(c)+\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(c^2-2sca+a^2) - 2 a \tau^\prime(a - sc) \\&=: g(a,c,s) \, . \end{align*} By \cref{mech:7}, $\partial_a g(a,c,s) \leq 0$. Thus, as $a \geq a_{\ms{min}} := (s+1)c/2$, we have $g(a,c,s) \leq g(a_{\ms{min}},c,s)$. Set $u := (1+s)c/2$, $v := (1-s)c/2$. Then $c = u+v$, $s = (u-v)/(u+v)$, $sc = u-v$, $u-sc=v$, and \begin{align*} g(a_{\ms{min}},c,s) &= g(u, u+v, (u-v)/(u+v)) \\&= \tau(u)-\tau(u+v)+\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(4uv + v^2) - 2 u \tau^\prime(v) \\&:= h(u, v) \, . \end{align*} By \cref{mech:8}, $\partial_u h(u, v) \leq 0$. Thus, as $u \geq 0$, we have \begin{align*} h(u, v) \leq h(0, v) = \tau(0) - \tau(v) + \tau(v) = 0 \, . \end{align*} Thus, $f(a,b,c,s) \leq g(a,c,s) \leq h(u, v) \leq 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Successive reductions in b, a and (u,v) via mech:6, mech:7, mech:8.
nodes.section: B.6 Proof of 9 lmm:param:firstreduction:a for $c \geq a$, $a \leq b$

nodes.name: partial_b f <= 0 (mech:6): reduce to b = a, giving g(a,c,s)
nodes.statement: Define \begin{equation*} f(a,b,c,s) := \tau(a)-\tau(c)-\tau(b-a)+\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(c^2-2scb+b^2) - 2 b \tau^\prime(a - sc) \, . \end{equation*} By \cref{mech:6}, $\partial_b f(a,b,c,s)\leq0$. Thus, as $b \geq a$, we have \begin{align*} f(a,b,c,s) &\leq f(a,a,c,s) \\&= \tau(a)-\tau(c)+\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(c^2-2sca+a^2) - 2 a \tau^\prime(a - sc) \\&=: g(a,c,s) \, . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: partial_b f <= 0 (mech:6): reduce to b = a, giving g(a,c,s)
nodes.section: B.6 Proof of 9 lmm:param:firstreduction:a for $c \geq a$, $a \leq b$

nodes.name: partial_a g <= 0 (mech:7): reduce to a = a_min
nodes.statement: By \cref{mech:7}, $\partial_a g(a,c,s) \leq 0$. Thus, as $a \geq a_{\ms{min}} := (s+1)c/2$, we have $g(a,c,s) \leq g(a_{\ms{min}},c,s)$.
nodes.statement_short: partial_a g <= 0 (mech:7): reduce to a = a_min
nodes.section: B.6 Proof of 9 lmm:param:firstreduction:a for $c \geq a$, $a \leq b$

nodes.name: Reparametrize as h(u,v)
nodes.statement: Set $u := (1+s)c/2$, $v := (1-s)c/2$. Then $c = u+v$, $s = (u-v)/(u+v)$, $sc = u-v$, $u-sc=v$, and \begin{align*} g(a_{\ms{min}},c,s) &= g(u, u+v, (u-v)/(u+v)) \\&= \tau(u)-\tau(u+v)+\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(4uv + v^2) - 2 u \tau^\prime(v) \\&:= h(u, v) \, . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Reparametrize as h(u,v)
nodes.section: B.6 Proof of 9 lmm:param:firstreduction:a for $c \geq a$, $a \leq b$

nodes.name: partial_u h <= 0 (mech:8), so f <= g <= h <= h(0,v) = 0
nodes.statement: By \cref{mech:8}, $\partial_u h(u, v) \leq 0$. Thus, as $u \geq 0$, we have \begin{align*} h(u, v) \leq h(0, v) = \tau(0) - \tau(v) + \tau(v) = 0 \, . \end{align*} Thus, $f(a,b,c,s) \leq g(a,c,s) \leq h(u, v) \leq 0$.
nodes.statement_short: partial_u h <= 0 (mech:8), so f <= g <= h <= h(0,v) = 0
nodes.section: B.6 Proof of 9 lmm:param:firstreduction:a for $c \geq a$, $a \leq b$

nodes.name: Lemma 9 (i) for a >= c, b <= 2sc, sc >= a-b
nodes.statement: Let $\tau\in\setccod3$. Let $a,b,c\in[0, \infty)$, $s\in[-1,1]$. Assume $\frac12 b \leq sc$, $sc \geq a-b$, and $a\geq c$. Then \begin{equation} \tau(a) - \tau(c) - \tau(a-b) + \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(c^2 - 2 s c b + b^2) \leq 2 b \tau^\prime\brOf{\frac{a-sc}{2}} \, . \end{equation}
nodes.section: B.7 Proof of 9 lmm:param:firstreduction:a for $a \geq c$, $b \leq 2sc$, $sc \geq a-b$
conclusions: \begin{equation} \tau(a) - \tau(c) - \tau(a-b) + \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(c^2 - 2 s c b + b^2) \leq 2 b \tau^\prime\brOf{\frac{a-sc}{2}} \, . \end{equation}
nodes.label: lmm:param:reduicLaLbscbLsc

nodes.name: Lemma 18 inequality
nodes.statement: \tau(a) - \tau(c) - \tau(a-b) + \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(c^2 - 2 s c b + b^2) \leq 2 b \tau^\prime\brOf{\frac{a-sc}{2}} \, .
nodes.section: B.7 Proof of 9 lmm:param:firstreduction:a for $a \geq c$, $b \leq 2sc$, $sc \geq a-b$
nodes.label: eq:reduicLaLbscbLsc:main

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 9 (i) for a >= c, b <= 2sc, sc >= a-b
nodes.statement: Define \begin{equation*} x_1^+ := a^2\, ,\qquad x_2^+ := c^2 - 2 s c b + b^2\, ,\qquad x_1^- := c^2\, ,\qquad x_2^- := (a-b)^2 \end{equation*} to write the left-hand side of \eqref{eq:reduicLaLbscbLsc:main} as \begin{equation*} \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(x_1^+) + \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(x_2^+) - \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(x_1^-) - \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(x_2^-) \, . \end{equation*} As $a\geq c$, \begin{equation} x_1^+ + x_2^+ - x_1^- - x_2^- = 2 b \br{a - s c} \geq 0 \, . \end{equation} Because $a \geq c$ and $b \leq 2sc$, we have $a-b \geq a-2sc \geq a-2c \geq -c$. Together with $a-b \leq a$, we obtain $x_1^+ \geq \max(x_1^-, x_2^-)$.\\ \underline{Case 1: $x_2^+ \geq \min(x_1^-, x_2^-)$:} By first applying \cref{lmm:f1} and then using \eqref{eq:reduicLaLbscbLsc:sqr}, we obtain \begin{equation*} \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(x_1^+) + \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(x_2^+) - \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(x_1^-) - \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(x_2^-) \leq 2 \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}\brOf{b \br{a - s c}} \, . \end{equation*} \underline{Case 2: $x_2^+ \leq \min(x_1^-, x_2^-)$:} By \eqref{eq:reduicLaLbscbLsc:sqr}, we have \begin{equation} x_1^+ + x_2^+ \geq x_1^- + x_2^- \, . \end{equation} By first applying \cref{lmm:f2}, then using \eqref{eq:reduicLaLbscbLsc:sqr}, and finally $\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}\smallfrown$, we obtain \begin{align*} &\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(x_1^+) + \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(x_2^+) - \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(x_1^-) - \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(x_2^-) \\&\leq \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}\brOf{2 b \br{a - s c}} \\&\leq 2\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}\brOf{b \br{a - s c}} \, . \end{align*} \underline{Finally:} The condition $0 \leq a-sc \leq b$ together with \cref{lmm:cc:transdtran} implies \begin{equation*} \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}\brOf{b \br{a - s c}} \leq b \tau^\prime\brOf{\frac{a-sc}{2}} \, . \qedhere \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Write the left side as a four-term tau_sqrt sum and use Lemmas 27/28, then Lemma 23.
nodes.section: B.7 Proof of 9 lmm:param:firstreduction:a for $a \geq c$, $b \leq 2sc$, $sc \geq a-b$

nodes.name: Rewrite the left side as a four-term tau_sqrt expression and order the arguments
nodes.statement: Define \begin{equation*} x_1^+ := a^2\, ,\qquad x_2^+ := c^2 - 2 s c b + b^2\, ,\qquad x_1^- := c^2\, ,\qquad x_2^- := (a-b)^2 \end{equation*} to write the left-hand side of \eqref{eq:reduicLaLbscbLsc:main} as \begin{equation*} \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(x_1^+) + \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(x_2^+) - \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(x_1^-) - \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(x_2^-) \, . \end{equation*} As $a\geq c$, \begin{equation} x_1^+ + x_2^+ - x_1^- - x_2^- = 2 b \br{a - s c} \geq 0 \, . \end{equation} Because $a \geq c$ and $b \leq 2sc$, we have $a-b \geq a-2sc \geq a-2c \geq -c$. Together with $a-b \leq a$, we obtain $x_1^+ \geq \max(x_1^-, x_2^-)$.
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite the left side as a four-term tau_sqrt expression and order the arguments
nodes.section: B.7 Proof of 9 lmm:param:firstreduction:a for $a \geq c$, $b \leq 2sc$, $sc \geq a-b$

nodes.name: Sum identity for x terms
nodes.section: B.7 Proof of 9 lmm:param:firstreduction:a for $a \geq c$, $b \leq 2sc$, $sc \geq a-b$
nodes.label: eq:reduicLaLbscbLsc:sqr

nodes.name: Lemma 27 bounds it by 2 tau_sqrt(b(a-sc))
nodes.statement: \underline{Case 1: $x_2^+ \geq \min(x_1^-, x_2^-)$:} By first applying \cref{lmm:f1} and then using \eqref{eq:reduicLaLbscbLsc:sqr}, we obtain \begin{equation*} \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(x_1^+) + \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(x_2^+) - \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(x_1^-) - \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(x_2^-) \leq 2 \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}\brOf{b \br{a - s c}} \, . \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 27 bounds it by 2 tau_sqrt(b(a-sc))
nodes.section: B.7 Proof of 9 lmm:param:firstreduction:a for $a \geq c$, $b \leq 2sc$, $sc \geq a-b$

nodes.name: Lemma 28 and concavity give the same bound
nodes.statement: \underline{Case 2: $x_2^+ \leq \min(x_1^-, x_2^-)$:} By \eqref{eq:reduicLaLbscbLsc:sqr}, we have \begin{equation} x_1^+ + x_2^+ \geq x_1^- + x_2^- \, . \end{equation} By first applying \cref{lmm:f2}, then using \eqref{eq:reduicLaLbscbLsc:sqr}, and finally $\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}\smallfrown$, we obtain \begin{align*} &\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(x_1^+) + \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(x_2^+) - \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(x_1^-) - \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(x_2^-) \\&\leq \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}\brOf{2 b \br{a - s c}} \\&\leq 2\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}\brOf{b \br{a - s c}} \, . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 28 and concavity give the same bound

nodes.name: x_1^+ + x_2^+ >= x_1^- + x_2^-
nodes.section: B.7 Proof of 9 lmm:param:firstreduction:a for $a \geq c$, $b \leq 2sc$, $sc \geq a-b$

nodes.name: Lemma 23 turns 2 tau_sqrt(b(a-sc)) into 2 b tau'((a-sc)/2)
nodes.statement: \underline{Finally:} The condition $0 \leq a-sc \leq b$ together with \cref{lmm:cc:transdtran} implies \begin{equation*} \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}\brOf{b \br{a - s c}} \leq b \tau^\prime\brOf{\frac{a-sc}{2}} \, . \qedhere \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 23 turns 2 tau_sqrt(b(a-sc)) into 2 b tau'((a-sc)/2)
nodes.section: B.7 Proof of 9 lmm:param:firstreduction:a for $a \geq c$, $b \leq 2sc$, $sc \geq a-b$

nodes.name: Lemma 9 (i) for a >= c, b >= 2sc
nodes.statement: Let $\tau\in\setccod3$. Let $a,b,c[0, \infty)$, $s\in[-1,1]$. Assume $b \geq 2sc$, $a\geq sc$. Then \begin{align*} \tau(a) - \tau(c) - \tau(\abs{a-b}) + \tau(c^2 - 2 s c b + b^2) \leq 2 \tau^\prime\brOf{\frac{a - s c}2} \, . \end{align*}
nodes.section: B.8 Proof of 9 lmm:param:firstreduction:a for $a \geq c$, $b \geq 2sc$
conclusions: \begin{align*} \tau(a) - \tau(c) - \tau(\abs{a-b}) + \tau(c^2 - 2 s c b + b^2) \leq 2 \tau^\prime\brOf{\frac{a - s c}2} \, . \end{align*}
nodes.label: lmm:param:reduicLabGsc

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 9 (i) for a >= c, b >= 2sc
nodes.statement: The function $x \mapsto \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(x+u) - \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(x)$, $u\geq0$ is $\searrow$ as $\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime\searrow$. Thus, \begin{align*} -\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(c^2) + \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(c^2 - 2 s c b+b^2) &\leq -\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}((sc)^2) + \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}((sc)^2 - 2 s c b+b^2) \\&= -\tau|sc| + \tau|sc-b| \, . \end{align*} We use this and then apply \cref{lmm:merging:simple} to obtain, \begin{align*} \tau(a) - \tau(c) - \tau|a-b| + \tau(c^2 - 2 s c b + b^2) &\leq \tau(a) - \tau|sc| - \tau|a-b| + \tau|sc-b| \\&\leq 2 \br{\tau\brOf{\frac{a - s c + b}2} - \tau\abs{\frac{a - s c - b}2}} \, . \end{align*} As $a - s c + b \geq \abs{a - s c - b}$, \cref{lmm:ccdiff} \ref{lmm:ccdiff:tightabs} yields \begin{align*} &\tau\brOf{\frac{a - s c + b}2} - \tau\abs{\frac{a - s c - b}2} \\&\leq \br{\frac{a - s c + b}2 - \frac{\abs{a - s c - b}}2} \tau^\prime\brOf{\frac{a - s c + b}4 + \frac{\abs{a - s c - b}}4} \\&\leq \min(a-sc, b) \tau^\prime\brOf{\frac{\max(a-sc, b)}2} \, . \end{align*} By \cref{lmm:tranconcave} \ref{lmm:tranconcave:balance}, \begin{equation} \min(a-sc, b) \tau^\prime\brOf{\frac{\max(a-sc, b)}2} \leq b \tau^\prime\brOf{\frac{a-sc}2} \, . \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Replace c-terms by sc-terms, apply the Simple Merging Lemma, then Lemmas 6 and 22.
nodes.section: B.8 Proof of 9 lmm:param:firstreduction:a for $a \geq c$, $b \geq 2sc$

nodes.name: Decreasing increments of tau_sqrt replace c by |sc|
nodes.statement: The function $x \mapsto \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(x+u) - \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(x)$, $u\geq0$ is $\searrow$ as $\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime\searrow$. Thus, \begin{align*} -\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(c^2) + \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(c^2 - 2 s c b+b^2) &\leq -\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}((sc)^2) + \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}((sc)^2 - 2 s c b+b^2) \\&= -\tau|sc| + \tau|sc-b| \, . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Decreasing increments of tau_sqrt replace c by |sc|
nodes.section: B.8 Proof of 9 lmm:param:firstreduction:a for $a \geq c$, $b \geq 2sc$

nodes.name: Apply the Simple Merging Lemma
nodes.statement: We use this and then apply \cref{lmm:merging:simple} to obtain, \begin{align*} \tau(a) - \tau(c) - \tau|a-b| + \tau(c^2 - 2 s c b + b^2) &\leq \tau(a) - \tau|sc| - \tau|a-b| + \tau|sc-b| \\&\leq 2 \br{\tau\brOf{\frac{a - s c + b}2} - \tau\abs{\frac{a - s c - b}2}} \, . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Apply the Simple Merging Lemma
nodes.section: B.8 Proof of 9 lmm:param:firstreduction:a for $a \geq c$, $b \geq 2sc$

nodes.name: Lemma 6 (ii) bounds the merged difference
nodes.statement: As $a - s c + b \geq \abs{a - s c - b}$, \cref{lmm:ccdiff} \ref{lmm:ccdiff:tightabs} yields \begin{align*} &\tau\brOf{\frac{a - s c + b}2} - \tau\abs{\frac{a - s c - b}2} \\&\leq \br{\frac{a - s c + b}2 - \frac{\abs{a - s c - b}}2} \tau^\prime\brOf{\frac{a - s c + b}4 + \frac{\abs{a - s c - b}}4} \\&\leq \min(a-sc, b) \tau^\prime\brOf{\frac{\max(a-sc, b)}2} \, . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 6 (ii) bounds the merged difference

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 9 (i) for a >= c, b <= 2sc, sc <= a-b
nodes.statement: Set $x:=a-b$. Define \begin{align*} f(x,b,c,s) := \tau(x+b)-\tau(c)-\tau(x)+\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(c^2 - 2 s c b + b^2) - 2 \br{ \tau\brOf{\frac{x - s c}{2} + b} - \tau\brOf{\frac{x - s c}{2}} } \, . \end{align*} Then \begin{equation*} \partial_x f(x,b,c,s) = \tau^\prime(x+b)-\tau^\prime(x) - \tau^\prime\brOf{\frac{x - s c}{2} + b} + \tau^\prime\brOf{\frac{x - s c}{2}} \, . \end{equation*} We have \begin{align*} x+b &\geq x\, ,& \frac{x - s c}{2} &\leq \frac{x - s c}{2} + b\, ,& (x+b) + \frac{x - s c}{2} &= x +\br{\frac{x - s c}{2} + b}\, . \end{align*} Thus, \cref{lmm:aux:extreme} implies \begin{equation*} \tau^\prime(x+b) + \tau^\prime\brOf{\frac{x - s c}{2}} \leq \tau^\prime(x) +\tau^\prime\brOf{\frac{x - s c}{2} + b} \, . \end{equation*} Thus, $\partial_x f(x,b,c,s) \leq 0$. Thus, as $x \geq sc$, we have $f(x,b,c,s) \leq f(sc, b,c,s)$. By \cref{lmm:xabc}, $f(sc, b,c,s) \leq 0$. Thus, $f(x,b,c,s) \leq 0$. Then we obtain, using \cref{lmm:ccdiff} \ref{lmm:ccdiff:tight} and $\tau^\prime\nearrow$, \begin{equation*} \tau(a) - \tau(c) - \tau(a-b) + \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(c^2 - 2 s c b + b^2) \leq 2 b \tau^\prime\brOf{\frac{a - s c}2} \, . \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Proof of Auxiliary inequality in x, b, c
nodes.statement: Define \begin{align*} f(x,b,c) &:= \tau(x+b) + \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(c^2 - 2 x b + b^2) - \tau(c) - \tau(x) - 2 \tau(b) \, , \\ g(x,b,c) := \partial_x f(x,b,c) &= \tau^\prime(x+b) - \tau^\prime(x) - 2b\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime(c^2 - 2 x b + b^2) \, . \end{align*} By \cref{mech:14}, $\partial_x g(x,b,c) \leq 0$. Thus, as $x \geq x_{\ms{min}} := \max(\frac b2, c-b)$, we have $g(x,b,c) \leq g(x_{\ms{min}},b,c)$. \\ \underline{Case 1, $x_{\ms{min}} = c-b$:}\\ In this case $c-b \geq b/2$, i.e., $2c\geq3b$. By \cref{mech:10}, $g(c-b, b, c) \leq 0$. Thus, as $x\geq x_{\ms{min}} = c-b$, we have $f(x,b,c) \leq f(c-b, b, c)$. By \cref{mech:11}, $f(c-b, b, c) \leq 0$. Thus, $f(x,b,c) \leq 0$. \\ \underline{Case 2, $x_{\ms{min}} = \frac b2$:}\\ In this case $c-b\leq b/2$, i.e., $2c \leq 3b$. By \cref{mech:12}, $g(b/2, b, c) \leq 0$. Thus, as $x\geq x_{\ms{min}} = b/2$, we have $f(x,b,c) \leq f(b/2, b, c)$. By \cref{mech:13}, $f(b/2, b, c) \leq 0$. Thus, $f(x,b,c) \leq 0$.

nodes.name: Proof of Simple properties of functions in S
nodes.statement: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item As $\tau$ and $\tau^\prime$ are convex and concave, respectively, we immediately obtain continuity on $(0, \infty)$. As $\tau$ is nondecreasing and convex, it must also be continuous at $0$. As $\tau$ is nondecreasing, $\tau^\prime$ is nonnegative. As $\tau$ is convex, $\tau^\prime$ is nondecreasing. Furthermore, $\lim_{x\searrow0} \tau^\prime(x)$ exists as $\tau^\prime$ is nonnegative and nondecreasing. Hence, by definition of $\tau^\prime(0)$, $\tau^\prime$ is continuous. As $\tau$ is convex and nondecreasing on $[0, \infty)$, \begin{equation} h\mapsto \frac{\tau(h)-\tau(0)}{h} \end{equation} is nondecreasing and nonnegative. Thus, $\partial_+ \tau(0)$ exists. It remains to show that $\partial_+ \tau(0) = \tau^\prime(0)$. Fix $\epsilon >0$. As $\tau^\prime$ is continuous, it is uniformly continuous on the compact interval $[0,2]$. Thus, we can find $\delta\in(0,1]$ such that $\abs{\tau^\prime(x)-\tau^\prime(y)} \leq \epsilon$ for all $x,y\in[0,2]$ with $0 < \abs{x-y} \leq \delta$. Thus, for any $h\in (0, \delta]$ and $x \in (0, 1]$, \begin{equation} \abs{\frac{\tau(x+h)-\tau(x)}{h} - \tau^\prime(x)} = \abs{\frac1h \int_0^h \tau^\prime(x+z) - \tau^\prime(x) \mathrm{d} z} \leq \epsilon \, . \end{equation} Choose $h\in (0, \delta]$ small enough such that, \begin{equation} \abs{\frac{\tau(h)-\tau(0)}{h} - \partial_+\tau(0)} \leq \epsilon \, . \end{equation} As $\tau$ is continuous and $h$ is fixed, we can find $x\in(0,1]$ small enough such that \begin{align*} \abs{\tau(x + h) - \tau(h)} &\leq h\epsilon\, ,\\ \abs{\tau(x) - \tau(0)} &\leq h\epsilon\, . \end{align*} Thus, we have \begin{align*} \abs{\tau^\prime(0) - \partial_+\tau(0)} &\leq \abs{\tau^\prime(0) - \tau^\prime(x)} + \abs{\tau^\prime(x) - \partial_+\tau(0)} \\&\epsilon + \abs{\tau^\prime(x) - \frac{\tau(x+h)-\tau(x)}{h}} + \abs{\frac{\tau(x+h)-\tau(x)}{h} - \partial_+\tau(0)} \\&2\epsilon + \abs{\frac{\tau(x+h)-\tau(x)}{h} - \frac{\tau(h)-\tau(0)}{h}}+ \abs{\frac{\tau(h)-\tau(0)}{h} - \partial_+\tau(0)} \\&3\epsilon + \frac1h\br{\abs{\tau(x+h)-\tau(h)}+\abs{\tau(x)-\tau(0)}} \\&\leq 5\epsilon \, . \end{align*} As $\epsilon > 0$ can be chosen arbitrarily small, $\tau^\prime(0) = \partial_+\tau(0)$. \item As $\tau$ is convex, $\tau^{\prime\prime}$ is nonnegative. As $\tau^\prime$ is concave, $\tau^{\prime\prime}$ is nonincreasing. \item As $\tau^\prime$ is concave, $\tau^{\prime\prime\prime}$ is nonpositive. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Elementary convexity arguments; an eps-argument identifies the right derivative at 0.

nodes.statement: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item[\ref{lmm:ccdiff:tight}] For the lower bound, as $\tau^\prime$ is concave, \begin{align*} \tau(x) - \tau(y) &= \int_y^x \tau^\prime(u) \mathrm{d} u \\&\geq (x-y)\int_0^1 (1-t)\tau^\prime(y) + t \tau^\prime(x)\, \mathrm{d} t \\&= \frac {x-y}2 \br{\tau^\prime(x)+\tau^\prime(y)} \, . \end{align*} For the upper bound, concavity of $\tau^\prime$ implies the existence of an affine linear function $h$ with $h(u) \geq \tau^\prime(u)$ for all $u \in[0, \infty)$ and \begin{equation} h\brOf{\frac{x+y}{2}} = \tau^\prime\brOf{\frac{x+y}{2}} \, . \end{equation} Thus, \begin{align*} \tau(x) - \tau(y) &\leq \int_y^x h(u) \mathrm{d} u \\&= \frac {x-y}2\br{h(x)+h(y)} \\&= (x-y) h\brOf{\frac{x+y}{2}} \, . \end{align*} \item[\ref{lmm:ccdiff:tightabs}] Follows directly from the upper bound in \ref{lmm:ccdiff:tight}. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Integrate tau' using concavity (chord below, tangent above).

nodes.name: (i) Lower and upper bounds
nodes.statement: [\ref{lmm:ccdiff:tight}] For the lower bound, as $\tau^\prime$ is concave, \begin{align*} \tau(x) - \tau(y) &= \int_y^x \tau^\prime(u) \mathrm{d} u \\&\geq (x-y)\int_0^1 (1-t)\tau^\prime(y) + t \tau^\prime(x)\, \mathrm{d} t \\&= \frac {x-y}2 \br{\tau^\prime(x)+\tau^\prime(y)} \, . \end{align*} For the upper bound, concavity of $\tau^\prime$ implies the existence of an affine linear function $h$ with $h(u) \geq \tau^\prime(u)$ for all $u \in[0, \infty)$ and \begin{equation} h\brOf{\frac{x+y}{2}} = \tau^\prime\brOf{\frac{x+y}{2}} \, . \end{equation} Thus, \begin{align*} \tau(x) - \tau(y) &\leq \int_y^x h(u) \mathrm{d} u \\&= \frac {x-y}2\br{h(x)+h(y)} \\&= (x-y) h\brOf{\frac{x+y}{2}} \, . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: (i) Lower and upper bounds
nodes.section: C.1 Nondecreasing, Convex Functions with Concave Derivative

nodes.name: Concave derivative
nodes.statement: Let $\tau\in\mc S$. \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item Let $x,y\in[0, \infty)$. Then \begin{equation*} \tau^\prime(x + y) \leq \tau^\prime(x) + \tau^\prime(y) \leq 2 \tau^\prime\brOf{\frac{x+y}2} \, . \end{equation*} \item Let $a,x\in[0, \infty)$. Then \begin{align*} \tau^\prime(ax) &\geq a\tau^\prime(x) \text{ for } a\leq 1\, ,\\ \tau^\prime(ax) &\leq a\tau^\prime(x) \text{ for } a\geq 1 \, . \end{align*} \item Let $x,y\in[0, \infty)$. Assume $y\geq x$. Then \begin{equation*} x \tau^\prime(y) \leq y \tau^\prime(x) \, . \end{equation*} \end{enumerate}
nodes.section: C.1 Nondecreasing, Convex Functions with Concave Derivative
conclusions: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item Let $x,y\in[0, \infty)$. Then \begin{equation*} \tau^\prime(x + y) \leq \tau^\prime(x) + \tau^\prime(y) \leq 2 \tau^\prime\brOf{\frac{x+y}2} \, . \end{equation*} \item Let $a,x\in[0, \infty)$. Then \begin{align*} \tau^\prime(ax) &\geq a\tau^\prime(x) \text{ for } a\leq 1\, ,\\ \tau^\prime(ax) &\leq a\tau^\prime(x) \text{ for } a\geq 1 \, . \end{align*} \item Let $x,y\in[0, \infty)$. Assume $y\geq x$. Then \begin{equation*} x \tau^\prime(y) \leq y \tau^\prime(x) \, . \end{equation*} \end{enumerate}
nodes.label: lmm:tranconcave

nodes.name: Proof of Concave derivative
nodes.statement: These are all well-known properties of nonnegative, concave functions. \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item Use \cref{lmm:aux:redistri} and Jensen's inequality. \item Use $(1-t)\tau^\prime(x_0) + t \tau^\prime(x_1) \leq \tau^\prime((1-t) x_0 + t x_1)$ on points $x_0=0$, $x_1=x$, $t = a$ and on $x_0=0$, $x_1=ax$, $t = 1/a$, respectively, and note that $\tau^\prime(0)\geq0$. \item Apply \ref{lmm:tranconcave:factor} with $a = y/x$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Standard properties of nonnegative concave functions via Lemma 24 and Jensen.

nodes.name: Square root and derivative
nodes.statement: Let $\tau\in\setccod2$. Let $x,y\in[0, \infty)$. Assume $x \geq y$. Then \begin{equation*} \tau\brOf{\sqrt{xy}} \leq x \tau^\prime\brOf{\frac12 y}\, . \end{equation*}
nodes.section: C.1 Nondecreasing, Convex Functions with Concave Derivative
conclusions: \begin{equation*} \tau\brOf{\sqrt{xy}} \leq x \tau^\prime\brOf{\frac12 y}\, . \end{equation*}
nodes.label: lmm:cc:transdtran

nodes.name: Proof of Square root and derivative
nodes.statement: Define $f(x, y) := x \tau^\prime(\frac12 y) - \tau(\sqrt{xy})$. Its partial derivative with respect to $x$ is \begin{align*} \partial_x f(x, y) &= \tau^\prime\brOf{\frac12 y} - \frac{\sqrt{y}}{2\sqrt{x}}\tau^\prime\brOf{\sqrt{xy}} \\&\geq \tau^\prime\brOf{\frac12 y} - \tau^\prime\brOf{\frac12 y} = 0 \, , \end{align*} by \cref{lmm:tranconcave} \ref{lmm:tranconcave:factor} with $\frac{\sqrt{y}}{2\sqrt{x}} \in [0,1]$. Thus, \begin{align*} f(x, y) &\geq f(y, y) \\&= y \tau^\prime\brOf{\frac12 y} - \tau(y) \\&\geq 0\, , \end{align*} where the last inequality is due to \cref{lmm:ccdiff} \ref{lmm:ccdiff:tight} with $\tau(0) = 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Monotonicity of f in x via Lemma 22 (ii), then Lemma 6 (i).

nodes.name: partial_x f >= 0 by Lemma 22 (ii)
nodes.statement: Define $f(x, y) := x \tau^\prime(\frac12 y) - \tau(\sqrt{xy})$. Its partial derivative with respect to $x$ is \begin{align*} \partial_x f(x, y) &= \tau^\prime\brOf{\frac12 y} - \frac{\sqrt{y}}{2\sqrt{x}}\tau^\prime\brOf{\sqrt{xy}} \\&\geq \tau^\prime\brOf{\frac12 y} - \tau^\prime\brOf{\frac12 y} = 0 \, , \end{align*} by \cref{lmm:tranconcave} \ref{lmm:tranconcave:factor} with $\frac{\sqrt{y}}{2\sqrt{x}} \in [0,1]$.
nodes.statement_short: partial_x f >= 0 by Lemma 22 (ii)

nodes.name: f(x,y) >= f(y,y) >= 0 by Lemma 6 (i)
nodes.statement: Thus, \begin{align*} f(x, y) &\geq f(y, y) \\&= y \tau^\prime\brOf{\frac12 y} - \tau(y) \\&\geq 0\, , \end{align*} where the last inequality is due to \cref{lmm:ccdiff} \ref{lmm:ccdiff:tight} with $\tau(0) = 0$.
nodes.statement_short: f(x,y) >= f(y,y) >= 0 by Lemma 6 (i)

nodes.name: Redistribution for concave and convex functions
nodes.statement: \mbox{ } \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item Let $f\colon[0, \infty) \to \mathbb{R}$. Assume $f$ is concave. Let $a,b\in[0, \infty)$ with $a\geq b$. Then $x \mapsto f(a+x) + f(b-x)$ is nonincreasing. If additionally $f(0)\geq 0$, then $f$ is subadditive. \item Let $f\colon[0, \infty) \to \mathbb{R}$. Assume $f$ is convex. Let $a,b\in[0, \infty)$ with $a\geq b$. Then $x \mapsto f(a+x) + f(b-x)$ is nondecreasing. \end{enumerate}
conclusions: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item Let $f\colon[0, \infty) \to \mathbb{R}$. Assume $f$ is concave. Let $a,b\in[0, \infty)$ with $a\geq b$. Then $x \mapsto f(a+x) + f(b-x)$ is nonincreasing. If additionally $f(0)\geq 0$, then $f$ is subadditive. \item Let $f\colon[0, \infty) \to \mathbb{R}$. Assume $f$ is convex. Let $a,b\in[0, \infty)$ with $a\geq b$. Then $x \mapsto f(a+x) + f(b-x)$ is nondecreasing. \end{enumerate}
nodes.label: lmm:aux:redistri

nodes.name: Proof of Redistribution for concave and convex functions
nodes.statement: We prove the first part; the second part is analogous. As $f$ is concave, we have \begin{align*} f(a) &\geq \frac{a-b+x}{a-b+2x} f(a+x) + \frac{x}{a-b+2x} f(b-x)\, ,\\ f(b) &\geq \frac{x}{a-b+2x} f(a+x) + \frac{a-b+x}{a-b+2x} f(b-x) \end{align*} for $x\in[0, b]$. Adding the two inequalities yields \begin{equation} f(a) + f(b) \geq f(a+x) + f(b-x) \, . \end{equation} As this inequality also applies to $\tilde a = a+x$, $\tilde b = b-x$, we have that $x \mapsto f(a+x) + f(b-x)$ is nonincreasing. Subadditivity follows by setting $x = b$.
nodes.statement_short: Add two concavity inequalities and iterate.

nodes.name: Prove the concave case; the convex one is analogous
nodes.statement: We prove the first part; the second part is analogous.
nodes.statement_short: Prove the concave case; the convex one is analogous

nodes.name: Two concavity inequalities sum to f(a)+f(b) >= f(a+x)+f(b-x)
nodes.statement: As $f$ is concave, we have \begin{align*} f(a) &\geq \frac{a-b+x}{a-b+2x} f(a+x) + \frac{x}{a-b+2x} f(b-x)\, ,\\ f(b) &\geq \frac{x}{a-b+2x} f(a+x) + \frac{a-b+x}{a-b+2x} f(b-x) \end{align*} for $x\in[0, b]$. Adding the two inequalities yields \begin{equation} f(a) + f(b) \geq f(a+x) + f(b-x) \, . \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Two concavity inequalities sum to f(a)+f(b) >= f(a+x)+f(b-x)

nodes.name: f(a)+f(b) >= f(a+x)+f(b-x)
nodes.statement: f(a) + f(b) \geq f(a+x) + f(b-x) \, .

nodes.name: Iterate to get monotonicity; x = b gives subadditivity
nodes.statement: As this inequality also applies to $\tilde a = a+x$, $\tilde b = b-x$, we have that $x \mapsto f(a+x) + f(b-x)$ is nonincreasing. Subadditivity follows by setting $x = b$.

nodes.name: Six-term inequality for nondecreasing concave functions
nodes.statement: Let $f\colon[0, \infty) \to \mathbb{R}$. Assume $f(0)\geq 0$, $f$ is nondecreasing, and $f$ is concave. Let $x_1, \dots, x_6 \in [0, \infty)$. Assume $\max(x_1, x_2, x_3, x_4) \leq \max(x_5, x_6)$ and $x_1+x_2+x_3+x_4 \geq x_5+x_6$. Then \begin{equation} f(x_1) + f(x_2) + f(x_3) + f(x_4) \geq f(x_5) + f(x_6) \, . \end{equation}
conclusions: \begin{equation} f(x_1) + f(x_2) + f(x_3) + f(x_4) \geq f(x_5) + f(x_6) \, . \end{equation}
nodes.label: lmm:aux:six

nodes.name: Proof of Six-term inequality for nondecreasing concave functions
nodes.statement: Without loss of generality assume $x_1 \geq x_2 \geq x_3 \geq x_4$ and $x_5\geq x_6$. First consider the case $x_1 \geq x_6$. We decrease $x_5$ and increase $x_6$ while holding $x_5+x_6$ constant until one $x_\bullet$ on the right-hand side coincides with one $x_\bullet$ one the left-hand side. By \cref{lmm:aux:redistri}, this can only increase the right-hand side of \eqref{eq:aux:six}. If $\{x_1, x_2, x_3, x_4\} \cap \{x_5, x_6\} \neq \emptyset$, we can subtract the term with the value in the intersection from \eqref{eq:aux:six}. The inequality of the form $f(x_1) + f(x_2) + f(x_3) \geq f(x_1 +x_2+x_3) \geq f(x_5)$ for $x_5 \leq x_1+x_2+x_3$ is obtained using subadditivity of $f$, see \cref{lmm:aux:redistri}, and the assumption that $f$ is nondecreasing. Now consider the case $x_1 < x_6$. Set $s := (x_5+x_6)/2$. Using \cref{lmm:aux:redistri}, we obtain $f(x_5) + f(x_6) \leq 2f(s)$. Furthermore $x_1 \leq s$ and $x_1 + x_2 + x_3 + x_4 \geq 2s$. Thus, again using \cref{lmm:aux:redistri} and the assumption that $f$ is nondecreasing, we can increase $x_1$ and $x_2$ while decreasing $x_3$ and $x_4$ to $0$ to get \begin{equation} f(x_1) + f(x_2) + f(x_3) + f(x_4) \geq 2f(s) + 2f(0) \, . \end{equation} As $f(0)\geq 0$, we arrive at the desired result.
nodes.statement_short: Case analysis; redistribute arguments via Lemma 24 and use subadditivity and monotonicity.

nodes.name: Order the variables
nodes.statement: Without loss of generality assume $x_1 \geq x_2 \geq x_3 \geq x_4$ and $x_5\geq x_6$.
nodes.statement_short: Order the variables

nodes.name: Case x_1 >= x_6: redistribute x_5, x_6 and cancel, then use subadditivity
nodes.statement: First consider the case $x_1 \geq x_6$. We decrease $x_5$ and increase $x_6$ while holding $x_5+x_6$ constant until one $x_\bullet$ on the right-hand side coincides with one $x_\bullet$ one the left-hand side. By \cref{lmm:aux:redistri}, this can only increase the right-hand side of \eqref{eq:aux:six}. If $\{x_1, x_2, x_3, x_4\} \cap \{x_5, x_6\} \neq \emptyset$, we can subtract the term with the value in the intersection from \eqref{eq:aux:six}. The inequality of the form $f(x_1) + f(x_2) + f(x_3) \geq f(x_1 +x_2+x_3) \geq f(x_5)$ for $x_5 \leq x_1+x_2+x_3$ is obtained using subadditivity of $f$, see \cref{lmm:aux:redistri}, and the assumption that $f$ is nondecreasing.
nodes.statement_short: Case x_1 >= x_6: redistribute x_5, x_6 and cancel, then use subadditivity

nodes.name: Case x_1 < x_6: compare both sides with 2 f(s)
nodes.statement: Now consider the case $x_1 < x_6$. Set $s := (x_5+x_6)/2$. Using \cref{lmm:aux:redistri}, we obtain $f(x_5) + f(x_6) \leq 2f(s)$. Furthermore $x_1 \leq s$ and $x_1 + x_2 + x_3 + x_4 \geq 2s$. Thus, again using \cref{lmm:aux:redistri} and the assumption that $f$ is nondecreasing, we can increase $x_1$ and $x_2$ while decreasing $x_3$ and $x_4$ to $0$ to get \begin{equation} f(x_1) + f(x_2) + f(x_3) + f(x_4) \geq 2f(s) + 2f(0) \, . \end{equation} As $f(0)\geq 0$, we arrive at the desired result.
nodes.statement_short: Case x_1 < x_6: compare both sides with 2 f(s)

nodes.name: Extreme-point inequality for tau'
nodes.statement: Let $\tau\in\mc S$. Let $a,b,c,d\in[0, \infty)$. Assume $a \geq b \geq c \geq d$ and $a+d \leq b+c$. Then $\tau^\prime(a) + \tau^\prime(d) \leq \tau^\prime(b) + \tau^\prime(c)$.
conclusions: $\tau^\prime(a) + \tau^\prime(d) \leq \tau^\prime(b) + \tau^\prime(c)$
nodes.label: lmm:aux:extreme

nodes.name: Proof of Extreme-point inequality for tau'
nodes.statement: As $\tau^\prime$ is concave, \cref{lmm:aux:redistri} applies.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 24 applied to the concave tau'.

nodes.name: Four-term bound for tau_sqrt (concavity)
nodes.statement: Let $\tau\in\setccod{3}$. Let $a\geq b\geq 0 $, $d \geq c \geq 0$. Then \begin{equation*} \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(a) - \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(b) - \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(c) + \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(d) \leq 2 \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}\brOf{\frac12 (a-b+d-c)} \, . \end{equation*}
conclusions: \begin{equation*} \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(a) - \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(b) - \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(c) + \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(d) \leq 2 \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}\brOf{\frac12 (a-b+d-c)} \, . \end{equation*}
nodes.label: lmm:f1

nodes.name: Proof of Four-term bound for tau_sqrt (concavity)
nodes.statement: As $a\geq b$, $d\geq c$, subadditivitiy of $\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}$ \begin{equation*} \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(a) - \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(b) - \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(c) + \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(d) \leq \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(a-b) + \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(d-c) \, . \end{equation*} Furthermore, by concavity of $\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}$, \begin{equation*} \frac12 \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(a-b) + \frac12 \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(d-c) \leq \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}\brOf{\frac12 (a-b+d-c)} \, . \qedhere \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Subadditivity and concavity of tau_sqrt.

nodes.name: Four-term bound for tau_sqrt (ordered arguments)
nodes.statement: Let $\tau\in\setccod{3}$. Let $a\geq b\geq c \geq d\geq 0$, $a+d\geq b+c$. Then \begin{equation*} \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(a) - \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(b) - \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(c) + \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(d) \leq \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(a-b-c+d) \, . \end{equation*}
conclusions: \begin{equation*} \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(a) - \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(b) - \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(c) + \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(d) \leq \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(a-b-c+d) \, . \end{equation*}
nodes.label: lmm:f2

nodes.name: Proof of Four-term bound for tau_sqrt (ordered arguments)
nodes.statement: Define $f(x,y) = \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(x) + \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(y) - \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(x + y)$ for $x,y\geq0$. Then $\partial_xf(x,y) = \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime(x) - \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime(x+y) \geq 0$ and similarly $\partial_yf(x,y) \geq 0$. Set $\delta := a-b$ and $\epsilon := c-d$. The assumptions ensure $\delta\geq\epsilon\geq0$. Then, \begin{equation*} f(b,\delta) \geq f(b,\epsilon) \geq f(d,\epsilon) \, . \end{equation*} Thus, \begin{align*} 0 &\geq f(d,\epsilon) - f(b,\delta) \\&= \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(d) + \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(\epsilon) - \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(d+\epsilon) - \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(b) - \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(\delta) + \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(b+\delta) \\&= \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(d) + \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(\epsilon) - \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(c) - \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(b) - \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(\delta) + \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(a) \, . \end{align*} With this we get \begin{align*} \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(d) - \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(c) - \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(b) + \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(a) &\leq \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(\delta) - \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(\epsilon) \\&\leq \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(\delta-\epsilon) \\&= \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(a-b-c+d) \, . \qedhere \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Monotonicity of f(x,y) = tau_sqrt(x)+tau_sqrt(y)-tau_sqrt(x+y) and subadditivity.

nodes.name: f(x,y) = tau_sqrt(x)+tau_sqrt(y)-tau_sqrt(x+y) is nondecreasing in both arguments
nodes.statement: Define $f(x,y) = \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(x) + \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(y) - \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(x + y)$ for $x,y\geq0$. Then $\partial_xf(x,y) = \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime(x) - \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime(x+y) \geq 0$ and similarly $\partial_yf(x,y) \geq 0$.
nodes.statement_short: f(x,y) = tau_sqrt(x)+tau_sqrt(y)-tau_sqrt(x+y) is nondecreasing in both arguments

nodes.name: With delta >= eps, monotonicity gives f(b,delta) >= f(d,eps)
nodes.statement: Set $\delta := a-b$ and $\epsilon := c-d$. The assumptions ensure $\delta\geq\epsilon\geq0$. Then, \begin{equation*} f(b,\delta) \geq f(b,\epsilon) \geq f(d,\epsilon) \, . \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: With delta >= eps, monotonicity gives f(b,delta) >= f(d,eps)

nodes.name: Expand the difference
nodes.statement: Thus, \begin{align*} 0 &\geq f(d,\epsilon) - f(b,\delta) \\&= \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(d) + \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(\epsilon) - \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(d+\epsilon) - \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(b) - \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(\delta) + \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(b+\delta) \\&= \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(d) + \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(\epsilon) - \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(c) - \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(b) - \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(\delta) + \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(a) \, . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Expand the difference

nodes.name: Subadditivity gives the bound by tau_sqrt(a-b-c+d)
nodes.statement: With this we get \begin{align*} \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(d) - \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(c) - \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(b) + \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(a) &\leq \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(\delta) - \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(\epsilon) \\&\leq \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(\delta-\epsilon) \\&= \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(a-b-c+d) \, . \qedhere \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Subadditivity gives the bound by tau_sqrt(a-b-c+d)

nodes.name: Simple Merging Lemma
nodes.statement: Let $\tau\in\setccod{3}$. Let $b\geq0$, $a,c\in\mathbb{R}$. Then \begin{equation*} \tau(|a|) - \tau(|c|) - \tau(|a-b|) + \tau(|c-b|) \leq 2 \br{ \tau\brOf{\frac{a - c + b}2} - \tau\brOf{\frac{|a-c - b|}2} } \indOf{a>c}\, . \end{equation*}
conclusions: \begin{equation*} \tau(|a|) - \tau(|c|) - \tau(|a-b|) + \tau(|c-b|) \leq 2 \br{ \tau\brOf{\frac{a - c + b}2} - \tau\brOf{\frac{|a-c - b|}2} } \indOf{a>c}\, . \end{equation*}
nodes.label: lmm:merging:simple

nodes.name: Proof of Simple Merging Lemma
nodes.statement: Define $f(x) := \tau(\abs{x}) - \tau(\abs{x - y})$. Then $f^\prime(x) = \mathsf{sgn}(x)\tau^\prime(\abs{x}) - \mathsf{sgn}(x)\tau^\prime(\abs{x - y})$. If $y \geq 0$ then: if $x \geq 0$ then $\abs{x} \geq \abs{x - y}$, if $x \leq 0$ then $\abs{x} \leq \abs{x - y}$. Thus, $f^\prime(x) \geq 0$, as $\tau^\prime$ is increasing. Hence, $f(x)$ is increasing. Thus, if $a\leq c$, then \begin{equation*} \tau(|a|)-\tau(|a-b|) \leq \tau(|c|) - \tau(|c-b|) \, . \end{equation*} This shows the inequality for the case $a\leq c$. Now assume $a>c$. Set $q := a-b$ and define \begin{equation*} g(b) := \tau(|q+b|) - \tau(|c|) - \tau(|q|) + \tau(|c-b|) - 2\br{\tau\brOf{\frac{q-c}{2}+b}-\tau\brOf{\frac{q-c}{2}}} \, . \end{equation*} We have \begin{equation*} g^\prime(b) = \mathsf{sgn}(q+b)\tau^\prime(|q+b|) - \mathsf{sgn}(c-b)\tau^\prime(|c-b|) - 2\tau^\prime\brOf{\frac{q-c}{2}+b} \, . \end{equation*} \underline{Case 1: $\mathsf{sgn}(q+b) = +1$, $\mathsf{sgn}(c-b)=+1$}: \begin{equation*} g^\prime(b) = \tau^\prime(q+b) - \tau^\prime(c-b) - 2\tau^\prime\brOf{\frac{q-c}{2}+b} \, , \end{equation*} As $\tau^\prime$ is concave, it is subadditive and $\tau^\prime(2x)\leq2\tau^\prime(x)$. Furthermore, $q+b = a > c \geq c-b$. Thus, \begin{equation*} \tau^\prime(q+b) - \tau^\prime(c-b) \leq \tau^\prime(q+b-c+b) \leq 2\tau^\prime\brOf{\frac{q-c}{2}+b} \, . \end{equation*} \underline{Case 2: $\mathsf{sgn}(q+b) = -1$, $\mathsf{sgn}(c-b)=-1$}: \begin{equation*} g^\prime(b) = -\tau^\prime(-q-b) + \tau^\prime(b - c) - 2\tau^\prime\brOf{\frac{q-c}{2}+b} \, , \end{equation*} Similarly to the first case, we have $b - c \geq -c > - a = - q - b$ and \begin{equation*} \tau^\prime(b - c)-\tau^\prime(-q-b) \leq \tau^\prime(b - c + q + b) \leq 2\tau^\prime\brOf{\frac{q-c}{2}+b} \, . \end{equation*} \underline{Case 3: $\mathsf{sgn}(q+b) = +1$, $\mathsf{sgn}(c-b)=-1$}: \begin{equation*} \tau^\prime(q+b) + \tau^\prime(b-c) - 2\tau^\prime\brOf{\frac{q-c}{2}+b} \, , \end{equation*} $\tau^\prime$ is concave, thus \begin{equation*} \frac 12 \tau^\prime(q+b) + \frac 12 \tau^\prime(b-c) \leq \tau^\prime\brOf{\frac{q-c}{2}+b} \, . \end{equation*} \underline{Case 4: $\mathsf{sgn}(q+b) = -1$, $\mathsf{sgn}(c-b)=+1$}: \begin{equation*} -\tau^\prime(-q-b) - \tau^\prime(c-b) - 2\tau^\prime\brOf{\frac{q-c}{2}+b} \, , \end{equation*} \begin{equation*} -\tau^\prime(-q-b)-\tau^\prime(c-b) \leq 0 \, . \end{equation*} \underline{Together:} In every case, we have $g^\prime(b) \leq 0$ and $g(0)=0$. Thus, \begin{equation*} g(b) \leq 0 \, . \qedhere \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Monotonicity for a <= c; for a > c a sign case analysis shows g' <= 0 with g(0) = 0.

nodes.name: Monotonicity of f handles a <= c; set up g(b) for a > c
nodes.statement: Define $f(x) := \tau(\abs{x}) - \tau(\abs{x - y})$. Then $f^\prime(x) = \mathsf{sgn}(x)\tau^\prime(\abs{x}) - \mathsf{sgn}(x)\tau^\prime(\abs{x - y})$. If $y \geq 0$ then: if $x \geq 0$ then $\abs{x} \geq \abs{x - y}$, if $x \leq 0$ then $\abs{x} \leq \abs{x - y}$. Thus, $f^\prime(x) \geq 0$, as $\tau^\prime$ is increasing. Hence, $f(x)$ is increasing. Thus, if $a\leq c$, then \begin{equation*} \tau(|a|)-\tau(|a-b|) \leq \tau(|c|) - \tau(|c-b|) \, . \end{equation*} This shows the inequality for the case $a\leq c$. Now assume $a>c$. Set $q := a-b$ and define \begin{equation*} g(b) := \tau(|q+b|) - \tau(|c|) - \tau(|q|) + \tau(|c-b|) - 2\br{\tau\brOf{\frac{q-c}{2}+b}-\tau\brOf{\frac{q-c}{2}}} \, . \end{equation*} We have \begin{equation*} g^\prime(b) = \mathsf{sgn}(q+b)\tau^\prime(|q+b|) - \mathsf{sgn}(c-b)\tau^\prime(|c-b|) - 2\tau^\prime\brOf{\frac{q-c}{2}+b} \, . \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Monotonicity of f handles a <= c; set up g(b) for a > c

nodes.name: Case a <= c: f(x) = tau(|x|) - tau(|x-y|) is increasing
nodes.statement: Define $f(x) := \tau(\abs{x}) - \tau(\abs{x - y})$. Then $f^\prime(x) = \mathsf{sgn}(x)\tau^\prime(\abs{x}) - \mathsf{sgn}(x)\tau^\prime(\abs{x - y})$. If $y \geq 0$ then: if $x \geq 0$ then $\abs{x} \geq \abs{x - y}$, if $x \leq 0$ then $\abs{x} \leq \abs{x - y}$. Thus, $f^\prime(x) \geq 0$, as $\tau^\prime$ is increasing. Hence, $f(x)$ is increasing. Thus, if $a\leq c$, then \begin{equation*} \tau(|a|)-\tau(|a-b|) \leq \tau(|c|) - \tau(|c-b|) \, . \end{equation*} This shows the inequality for the case $a\leq c$.
nodes.statement_short: Case a <= c: f(x) = tau(|x|) - tau(|x-y|) is increasing

nodes.name: Case a > c: define g(b) and its derivative
nodes.statement: Now assume $a>c$. Set $q := a-b$ and define \begin{equation*} g(b) := \tau(|q+b|) - \tau(|c|) - \tau(|q|) + \tau(|c-b|) - 2\br{\tau\brOf{\frac{q-c}{2}+b}-\tau\brOf{\frac{q-c}{2}}} \, . \end{equation*} We have \begin{equation*} g^\prime(b) = \mathsf{sgn}(q+b)\tau^\prime(|q+b|) - \mathsf{sgn}(c-b)\tau^\prime(|c-b|) - 2\tau^\prime\brOf{\frac{q-c}{2}+b} \, . \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Case a > c: define g(b) and its derivative

nodes.name: Signs (+,+): subadditivity of tau'
nodes.statement: \underline{Case 1: $\mathsf{sgn}(q+b) = +1$, $\mathsf{sgn}(c-b)=+1$}: \begin{equation*} g^\prime(b) = \tau^\prime(q+b) - \tau^\prime(c-b) - 2\tau^\prime\brOf{\frac{q-c}{2}+b} \, , \end{equation*} As $\tau^\prime$ is concave, it is subadditive and $\tau^\prime(2x)\leq2\tau^\prime(x)$. Furthermore, $q+b = a > c \geq c-b$. Thus, \begin{equation*} \tau^\prime(q+b) - \tau^\prime(c-b) \leq \tau^\prime(q+b-c+b) \leq 2\tau^\prime\brOf{\frac{q-c}{2}+b} \, . \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Signs (+,+): subadditivity of tau'

nodes.name: Signs (-,-): same argument
nodes.statement: \underline{Case 2: $\mathsf{sgn}(q+b) = -1$, $\mathsf{sgn}(c-b)=-1$}: \begin{equation*} g^\prime(b) = -\tau^\prime(-q-b) + \tau^\prime(b - c) - 2\tau^\prime\brOf{\frac{q-c}{2}+b} \, , \end{equation*} Similarly to the first case, we have $b - c \geq -c > - a = - q - b$ and \begin{equation*} \tau^\prime(b - c)-\tau^\prime(-q-b) \leq \tau^\prime(b - c + q + b) \leq 2\tau^\prime\brOf{\frac{q-c}{2}+b} \, . \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Signs (-,-): same argument

nodes.name: Signs (+,-): concavity of tau'
nodes.statement: \underline{Case 3: $\mathsf{sgn}(q+b) = +1$, $\mathsf{sgn}(c-b)=-1$}: \begin{equation*} \tau^\prime(q+b) + \tau^\prime(b-c) - 2\tau^\prime\brOf{\frac{q-c}{2}+b} \, , \end{equation*} $\tau^\prime$ is concave, thus \begin{equation*} \frac 12 \tau^\prime(q+b) + \frac 12 \tau^\prime(b-c) \leq \tau^\prime\brOf{\frac{q-c}{2}+b} \, . \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Signs (+,-): concavity of tau'

nodes.name: Signs (-,+): trivially nonpositive
nodes.statement: \underline{Case 4: $\mathsf{sgn}(q+b) = -1$, $\mathsf{sgn}(c-b)=+1$}: \begin{equation*} -\tau^\prime(-q-b) - \tau^\prime(c-b) - 2\tau^\prime\brOf{\frac{q-c}{2}+b} \, , \end{equation*} \begin{equation*} -\tau^\prime(-q-b)-\tau^\prime(c-b) \leq 0 \, . \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Signs (-,+): trivially nonpositive

nodes.name: g' <= 0 and g(0) = 0, so g <= 0
nodes.statement: \underline{Together:} In every case, we have $g^\prime(b) \leq 0$ and $g(0)=0$. Thus, \begin{equation*} g(b) \leq 0 \, . \qedhere \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Mechanical lemma mech:1
nodes.statement: Let $\tau\in\setccod3$. Let $a,b,c\in[0, \infty)$. Assume $a\geq c$, $a-b-2c \geq 0$. Then \begin{equation} 2(a-b-2c)\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime((a-b)^2+4cb) + \tau^\prime(c+b) - 2 \tau^\prime(a - c) \leq 0 \, . \end{equation}
conclusions: \begin{equation} 2(a-b-2c)\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime((a-b)^2+4cb) + \tau^\prime(c+b) - 2 \tau^\prime(a - c) \leq 0 \, . \end{equation}
nodes.label: mech:1

nodes.name: Mechanical inequality 1
nodes.statement: 2(a-b-2c)\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime((a-b)^2+4cb) + \tau^\prime(c+b) - 2 \tau^\prime(a - c) \leq 0 \, .

nodes.name: Proof of Mechanical lemma mech:1
nodes.statement: \begin{align*} & 2(a-b-2c)\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime((a-b)^2+4cb) + \tau^\prime(c+b) - 2 \tau^\prime(a - c) \\ \tau^\prime\geq0 \qquad&\leq 2(a-b-2c)\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime((a-b)^2+4cb) - \tau^\prime(a - c) \\ \qquad&= 2(a-b)\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime((a-b)^2+4cb) -4c\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime((a-b)^2+4cb) - \tau^\prime(a - c) \\ a\geq b,\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime\searrow \qquad&\leq 2(a-b)\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime((a-b)^2) -4c\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime((a-b)^2+4cb) - \tau^\prime(a - c) \\ \qquad&= \tau^\prime(a-b) - 4c\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime(a^2 - b((a-2c)+(a-b-2c))) - \tau^\prime(a - c) \\ a-2c\geq b\geq0,\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime\searrow \qquad&\leq \tau^\prime(a-b) - 4c\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime(a^2) - \tau^\prime(a - c) \\ \qquad&= \tau^\prime(a-b) - \frac{2c}a \tau^\prime(a) - \tau^\prime(a - c) \\ \tau^\prime\nearrow \qquad&\leq \tau^\prime(a) - \frac{2c}a \tau^\prime(a) - \tau^\prime(a - c) \\ \qquad&= \br{1 - \frac{2c}a} \tau^\prime(a) - \tau^\prime(a - c) \\ a\geq2c, \tau^\prime\smallfrown \qquad&\leq \tau^\prime\brOf{\br{1 - \frac{2c}a}a} - \tau^\prime(a - c) \\ \qquad&= \tau^\prime\brOf{a-2c} - \tau^\prime(a - c) \\ \tau^\prime\nearrow \qquad&\leq 0 \, . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Chain of elementary inequalities using monotonicity, convexity or concavity of tau', tau'' and tau_sqrt'.

nodes.name: Mechanical lemma mech:2
nodes.statement: Let $\tau\in\setccod3$. Let $a,b,c\in[0, \infty)$. Assume $a\geq c$, $a-b-2c \leq 0$. Then \begin{equation} -2(b+2c-a)\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime((a-b)^2+4cb) + \tau^\prime(c+b) - 2 \tau^\prime(a - c) \leq 0 \, . \end{equation}
conclusions: \begin{equation} -2(b+2c-a)\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime((a-b)^2+4cb) + \tau^\prime(c+b) - 2 \tau^\prime(a - c) \leq 0 \, . \end{equation}
nodes.label: mech:2

nodes.name: Mechanical inequality 2
nodes.statement: -2(b+2c-a)\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime((a-b)^2+4cb) + \tau^\prime(c+b) - 2 \tau^\prime(a - c) \leq 0 \, .

nodes.name: Proof of Mechanical lemma mech:2
nodes.statement: \begin{align*} & -2(b+2c-a)\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime((a-b)^2+4cb) + \tau^\prime(c+b) - 2 \tau^\prime(a - c) \\ \qquad&= -2(b+2c-a)\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime(a^2 + b(-2a + b + 4c)) + \tau^\prime(c+b) - 2 \tau^\prime(a - c) \\ a \geq c, b+2c\geq a, \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime\searrow \qquad&\leq -2(b+2c-a)\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime(a^2 + b(-2a + b + 4a)) + \tau^\prime(c+b) - 2 \tau^\prime(a - c) \\ \qquad&= -2(b+2c-a)\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime((a+b)^2) + \tau^\prime(c+b) - 2 \tau^\prime(a - c) \\ \qquad&= -\frac{b+2c-a}{a+b}\tau^\prime(a+b) + \tau^\prime(c+b) - 2 \tau^\prime(a - c) \\ a \geq c, \tau^\prime\nearrow \qquad&\leq -\frac{b+2c-a}{a+b}\tau^\prime(a+b) + \tau^\prime(a+b) - 2 \tau^\prime(a - c) \\ \qquad&= \frac{2(a-c)}{a+b}\tau^\prime(a+b) - 2 \tau^\prime(a - c) \\ 0 \leq a-c \leq a+b, \tau^\prime\smallfrown \qquad&\leq 2\tau^\prime(a-c) - 2 \tau^\prime(a - c) \\ \qquad&= 0 \, . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Chain of elementary inequalities using monotonicity, convexity or concavity of tau', tau'' and tau_sqrt'.

nodes.name: Mechanical lemma mech:3
nodes.statement: Let $\tau\in\setccod3$. Let $a,b,c\geq0$, $s\in[-1,1]$. Assume $a \geq b \geq sc$. Then \begin{equation*} \tau^\prime(a-b) + 2(b-sc)\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime(c^2-2scb+b^2) - 2 \tau^\prime(a - sc) \leq 0 \, . \end{equation*}
conclusions: \begin{equation*} \tau^\prime(a-b) + 2(b-sc)\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime(c^2-2scb+b^2) - 2 \tau^\prime(a - sc) \leq 0 \, . \end{equation*}
nodes.label: mech:3

nodes.name: Proof of Mechanical lemma mech:3
nodes.statement: \begin{align*} & \tau^\prime(a-b) + 2(b-sc)\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime(c^2-2scb+b^2) - 2 \tau^\prime(a - sc) \\ c\geq sc, \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime\searrow \qquad&\leq \tau^\prime(a-b) + 2(b-sc)\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime(s^2c^2-2scb+b^2) - 2 \tau^\prime(a - sc) \\ \qquad&= \tau^\prime(a-b) + \tau^\prime(b-sc) - 2 \tau^\prime(a - sc) \\ a \geq b \geq sc, \tau^\prime\nearrow \qquad&\leq \tau^\prime(a-sc) + \tau^\prime(a-sc) - 2 \tau^\prime(a - sc) \\ \qquad&= 0 \, . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Chain of elementary inequalities using monotonicity, convexity or concavity of tau', tau'' and tau_sqrt'.

nodes.name: Mechanical lemma mech:5
nodes.statement: Let $\tau\in\setccod3$. Let $u,v\in[0, \infty)$. Assume $u \geq v$. Then \begin{equation*} \tau^\prime(u)-\tau^\prime(u+v)+4v\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime(4uv) - 2\tau^\prime(v) \leq 0 \, . \end{equation*}
conclusions: \begin{equation*} \tau^\prime(u)-\tau^\prime(u+v)+4v\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime(4uv) - 2\tau^\prime(v) \leq 0 \, . \end{equation*}
nodes.label: mech:5

nodes.name: Proof of Mechanical lemma mech:5
nodes.statement: \begin{align*} & \tau^\prime(u)-\tau^\prime(u+v)+4v\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime(4uv) - 2\tau^\prime(v) \\ \tau^\prime\nearrow \qquad&\leq 4v\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime(4uv) - 2\tau^\prime(v) \\ u\geq v, \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime\searrow \qquad&\leq 4v\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime(4vv) - 2\tau^\prime(v) \\ \qquad&= \tau^\prime(2v) - 2\tau^\prime(v) \\ \tau^\prime\smallfrown \qquad&\leq 0 \, . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Chain of elementary inequalities using monotonicity, convexity or concavity of tau', tau'' and tau_sqrt'.

nodes.name: Mechanical lemma mech:6
nodes.statement: Let $\tau\in\setccod3$. Let $a,b,c\geq0$, $s\in[-1,1]$. Assume $(s+1)c\leq 2a$, $a \leq b$. Then \begin{equation*} -\tau^\prime(b-a)+2(b-sc)\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime(c^2-2scb+b^2) - 2\tau^\prime(a - sc) \leq 0 \, . \end{equation*}
conclusions: \begin{equation*} -\tau^\prime(b-a)+2(b-sc)\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime(c^2-2scb+b^2) - 2\tau^\prime(a - sc) \leq 0 \, . \end{equation*}
nodes.label: mech:6

nodes.name: Proof of Mechanical lemma mech:6
nodes.statement: \begin{align*} & -\tau^\prime(b-a)+2(b-sc)\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime(c^2-2scb+b^2) - 2\tau^\prime(a - sc) \\ \tau^\prime\smallfrown \text{(subadditiv)} \qquad&\leq -\tau^\prime(b-a + 2(a - sc))+2(b-sc)\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime(c^2-2scb+b^2) \\ \qquad&= -\tau^\prime(b+a-2sc) + 2(b-sc)\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime(c^2-2scb+b^2) \\ a \geq \frac{1+s}{2}c,\tau^\prime\nearrow \qquad&\leq -\tau^\prime(b+\frac{1+s}{2}c-2sc) + 2(b-sc)\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime(c^2-2scb+b^2) \\ \qquad&= -\tau^\prime(b+\frac{1-s}{2}c-sc) + 2(b-sc)\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime(c^2-2scb+b^2) \\ 1-s \geq 0,\tau^\prime\nearrow \qquad&\leq -\tau^\prime(b-sc) + 2(b-sc)\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime(c^2-2scb+b^2) \\ sc \leq c,\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime\searrow \qquad&\leq -\tau^\prime(b-sc) + 2(b-sc)\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime((sc)^2-2scb+b^2) \\ \qquad&= -\tau^\prime(b-sc) + \tau^\prime(b-sc) \\ \qquad&= 0 \, . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Chain of elementary inequalities using monotonicity, convexity or concavity of tau', tau'' and tau_sqrt'.

nodes.name: Mechanical lemma mech:7
nodes.statement: Let $\tau\in\setccod3$. Let $a,c\in[0, \infty)$, $s\in[-1,1]$. Assume $a \geq sc$. Then \begin{equation*} \tau^\prime(a) + 2(a-sc)\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime(c^2-2sca+a^2) - 2 \tau^\prime(a - sc) - 2 a \tau^{\prime\prime}(a - sc) \leq 0 \, . \end{equation*}
conclusions: \begin{equation*} \tau^\prime(a) + 2(a-sc)\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime(c^2-2sca+a^2) - 2 \tau^\prime(a - sc) - 2 a \tau^{\prime\prime}(a - sc) \leq 0 \, . \end{equation*}
nodes.label: mech:7

nodes.name: Proof of Mechanical lemma mech:7
nodes.statement: \begin{align*} & \tau^\prime(a) + 2(a-sc)\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime(c^2-2sca+a^2) - 2 \tau^\prime(a - sc) - 2 a \tau^{\prime\prime}(a - sc) \\ a \geq sc, sc \leq c, \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime\searrow \qquad&\leq \tau^\prime(a) + 2(a-sc)\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime((sc)^2-2sca+a^2) - 2 \tau^\prime(a - sc) - 2 a \tau^{\prime\prime}(a - sc) \\ \qquad&= \tau^\prime(a) + \tau^\prime(a - sc) - 2 \tau^\prime(a - sc) - 2 a \tau^{\prime\prime}(a - sc) \\ \qquad&= \tau^\prime(a) - \tau^\prime(a - sc) - 2 a \tau^{\prime\prime}(a - sc) \\ sc \leq 2 a, \tau^{\prime\prime}\geq0 \qquad&\leq \tau^\prime(a) - \tau^\prime(a - sc) - sc \tau^{\prime\prime}(a - sc) \\ \text{\cref{lmm:ccpoly} \ref{lmm:ccpoly:dtaylor}} \qquad&\leq 0 \, . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Chain of elementary inequalities using monotonicity, convexity or concavity of tau', tau'' and tau_sqrt'.

nodes.name: Mechanical lemma mech:8
nodes.statement: Let $\tau\in\setccod3$. Let $u,v\in[0, \infty)$. Then \begin{equation*} \tau^\prime(u) - \tau^\prime(u+v) + 4v\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime(4uv + v^2) - 2\tau^\prime(v) \leq 0 \, . \end{equation*}
conclusions: \begin{equation*} \tau^\prime(u) - \tau^\prime(u+v) + 4v\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime(4uv + v^2) - 2\tau^\prime(v) \leq 0 \, . \end{equation*}
nodes.label: mech:8

nodes.name: Proof of Mechanical lemma mech:8
nodes.statement: \begin{align*} &\tau^\prime(u) - \tau^\prime(u+v) + 4v\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime(4uv + v^2) - 2\tau^\prime(v) \\ \qquad&= \tau^\prime(u) - \tau^\prime(u+v) + \frac{1}{\sqrt{u/v + 1/4}}\tau^\prime(2v\sqrt{u/v + 1/4}) - 2\tau^\prime(v) \\ 2\sqrt{u/v + 1/4}\geq 1, \tau^\prime\smallfrown \qquad&\leq \tau^\prime(u) - \tau^\prime(u+v) + \frac{2\sqrt{u/v + 1/4}}{\sqrt{u/v + 1/4}}\tau^\prime(v) - 2\tau^\prime(v) \\ \qquad&= \tau^\prime(u)-\tau^\prime(u+v) \\ v\geq0, \tau^\prime\nearrow \qquad&\leq 0 \, . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Chain of elementary inequalities using monotonicity, convexity or concavity of tau', tau'' and tau_sqrt'.

nodes.name: Mechanical lemma mech:9
nodes.statement: Let $\tau\in\setccod3$. Let $a,b,c\in[0, \infty)$ and $s\in[-1,1]$. Assume $a \geq sc \geq b$. Then \begin{equation*} \tau^\prime(a) - \tau^\prime(a-b) - 2b \tau^{\prime\prime}(a - sc) \leq 0 \, . \end{equation*}
conclusions: \begin{equation*} \tau^\prime(a) - \tau^\prime(a-b) - 2b \tau^{\prime\prime}(a - sc) \leq 0 \, . \end{equation*}
nodes.label: mech:9

nodes.name: Proof of Mechanical lemma mech:9
nodes.statement: \begin{align*} & \tau^\prime(a) - \tau^\prime(a-b) - 2b \tau^{\prime\prime}(a - sc) \\ b\leq sc, \tau^{\prime\prime}\searrow \qquad&\leq \tau^\prime(a) - \tau^\prime(a-b) - 2b \tau^{\prime\prime}(a - b) \\ \text{\cref{lmm:ccpoly} \ref{lmm:ccpoly:dtaylor}} \qquad&\leq b \tau^{\prime\prime}(a - b) - 2b \tau^{\prime\prime}(a - b) \\ \qquad&= -b \tau^{\prime\prime}(a - b) \\ \tau^{\prime\prime}\geq0 \qquad&\leq 0 \, . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Chain of elementary inequalities using monotonicity, convexity or concavity of tau', tau'' and tau_sqrt'.

nodes.name: Mechanical lemma mech:10
nodes.statement: Let $\tau\in\setccod3$. Let $b,c\in[0, \infty)$. Assume $2c\geq3b$. Then \begin{equation*} \tau^\prime(c) - \tau^\prime(c-b) - 2b \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime(c^2 - 2 (c-b) b + b^2) \leq 0 \, . \end{equation*}
conclusions: \begin{equation*} \tau^\prime(c) - \tau^\prime(c-b) - 2b \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime(c^2 - 2 (c-b) b + b^2) \leq 0 \, . \end{equation*}
nodes.label: mech:10

nodes.name: Proof of Mechanical lemma mech:10
nodes.statement: \begin{align*} &\tau^\prime(c) - \tau^\prime(c-b) - 2b \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime(c^2 - 2 (c-b) b + b^2) \\ \qquad&= \tau^\prime(c)- \tau^\prime(c-b) - 2b \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime(c^2 - b (2c-3b)) \\ 2c\geq3b, \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime\searrow \qquad&\leq \tau^\prime(c)- \tau^\prime(c-b) - 2b \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime(c^2) \\ \qquad&= \tau^\prime(c)- \tau^\prime(c-b) - \frac bc \tau^\prime(c) \\ \qquad&= \frac{c-b}{c}\tau^\prime(c) - \tau^\prime(c-b) \\ \frac{c-b}{c}\in[0,1], \tau^\prime\smallfrown \qquad&\leq \tau^\prime(c-b) - \tau^\prime(c-b) \\ \qquad&= 0 \, . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Chain of elementary inequalities using monotonicity, convexity or concavity of tau', tau'' and tau_sqrt'.

nodes.name: Mechanical lemma mech:11
nodes.statement: Let $\tau\in\setccod3$. Let $b,c\in[0, \infty)$. Assume $c\geq b$. Then \begin{equation*} \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}((c-b)^2 + 2 b^2) - \tau(c-b) - 2\tau(b) \leq 0 \, . \end{equation*}
conclusions: \begin{equation*} \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}((c-b)^2 + 2 b^2) - \tau(c-b) - 2\tau(b) \leq 0 \, . \end{equation*}
nodes.label: mech:11

nodes.name: Proof of Mechanical lemma mech:11
nodes.statement: \begin{align*} &\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}((c-b)^2 + 2 b^2) - \tau(c-b) - 2\tau(b) \\ \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}\smallfrown\text{ (subadditive)} \qquad&\leq \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}((c-b)^2) + \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(2 b^2) - \tau(c-b) - 2\tau(b) \\ \qquad&= \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(2b^2) - 2\tau(b) \\ \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}\smallfrown\text{ (subadditive)} \qquad&\leq \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(b^2) + \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(b^2) - 2\tau(b) \\ \qquad&= 0 \, . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Chain of elementary inequalities using monotonicity, convexity or concavity of tau', tau'' and tau_sqrt'.

nodes.name: Mechanical lemma mech:12
nodes.statement: Let $\tau\in\setccod3$. Let $b,c\in[0, \infty)$. Assume $2c \leq 3b$. Then \begin{equation*} \tau^\prime\brOf{\frac32 b} - \tau^\prime\brOf{\frac12 b} - 2b \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime(c^2) \leq 0 \, . \end{equation*}
conclusions: \begin{equation*} \tau^\prime\brOf{\frac32 b} - \tau^\prime\brOf{\frac12 b} - 2b \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime(c^2) \leq 0 \, . \end{equation*}
nodes.label: mech:12

nodes.name: Proof of Mechanical lemma mech:12
nodes.statement: \begin{align*} &\tau^\prime\brOf{\frac32 b} - \tau^\prime\brOf{\frac12 b} - 2b \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime(c^2) \\ c \leq \frac32b, \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime\searrow \qquad&\leq \tau^\prime\brOf{\frac32 b} - \tau^\prime\brOf{\frac12 b} - 2b \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime\brOf{\br{\frac32 b}^2} \\ \qquad&= \tau^\prime\brOf{\frac32 b} - \tau^\prime\brOf{\frac12 b} - \frac23 \tau^\prime\brOf{\frac32 b} \\ \qquad&= \frac13\tau^\prime\brOf{\frac32 b} - \tau^\prime\brOf{\frac12 b} \\ \frac13\leq 1,\tau^\prime\smallfrown \qquad&\leq \tau^\prime\brOf{\frac12 b} - \tau^\prime\brOf{\frac12 b} \\ \qquad&= 0\, . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Chain of elementary inequalities using monotonicity, convexity or concavity of tau', tau'' and tau_sqrt'.

nodes.name: Mechanical lemma mech:13
nodes.statement: Let $\tau\in\setccod3$. Let $b\in[0, \infty)$. Then \begin{equation*} \tau(\frac32 b) - \tau(\frac 12 b) - 2 \tau(b) \leq 0 \, . \end{equation*}
conclusions: \begin{equation*} \tau(\frac32 b) - \tau(\frac 12 b) - 2 \tau(b) \leq 0 \, . \end{equation*}
nodes.label: mech:13

nodes.name: Proof of Mechanical lemma mech:13
nodes.statement: \begin{align*} &\tau(\frac32 b) - \tau(\frac 12 b) - 2 \tau(b) \\ \qquad&= \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(\frac94 b^2) - \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(\frac 14 b^2) - 2 \tau(b) \\ \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}\smallfrown\text{ (subadditive)} \qquad&\leq \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(\frac84 b^2) - 2 \tau(b) \\ \qquad&= \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(2 b^2) - 2 \tau(b) \\ \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}\smallfrown\text{ (subadditive)} \qquad&\leq \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(b^2) + \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}(b^2) - 2 \tau(b) \\ \qquad&= 0 \, . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Chain of elementary inequalities using monotonicity, convexity or concavity of tau', tau'' and tau_sqrt'.

nodes.name: Mechanical lemma mech:14
nodes.statement: Let $\tau\in\setccod3$. Let $x,b,c\in[0, \infty)$. Assume $x \leq c$. Then \begin{equation*} \tau^{\prime\prime}(x+b) - \tau^{\prime\prime}(x) + 4 b^2\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^{\prime\prime}(c^2 - 2 x b + b^2) \leq 0 \, . \end{equation*}
conclusions: \begin{equation*} \tau^{\prime\prime}(x+b) - \tau^{\prime\prime}(x) + 4 b^2\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^{\prime\prime}(c^2 - 2 x b + b^2) \leq 0 \, . \end{equation*}
nodes.label: mech:14

nodes.name: Proof of Mechanical lemma mech:14
nodes.statement: \begin{align*} & \tau^{\prime\prime}(x+b) - \tau^{\prime\prime}(x) + 4 b^2\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^{\prime\prime}(c^2 - 2 x b + b^2) \\ \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^{\prime\prime}\leq0 \qquad&\leq \tau^{\prime\prime}(x+b) - \tau^{\prime\prime}(x) \\ \tau^{\prime\prime}\searrow \qquad&\leq 0 \, . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Chain of elementary inequalities using monotonicity, convexity or concavity of tau', tau'' and tau_sqrt'.

nodes.name: Mechanical lemma mech:15
nodes.statement: Let $\tau\in\setccod3$. Let $u,c\in[0, \infty)$. Then \begin{equation*} 2\tau^\prime(u) - 2\tau^\prime(u/2) - \frac u2 \tau^{\prime\prime}(c) - u\tau^{\prime\prime}(u/2) \leq 0 \, . \end{equation*}
conclusions: \begin{equation*} 2\tau^\prime(u) - 2\tau^\prime(u/2) - \frac u2 \tau^{\prime\prime}(c) - u\tau^{\prime\prime}(u/2) \leq 0 \, . \end{equation*}
nodes.label: mech:15

nodes.name: Proof of Mechanical lemma mech:15
nodes.statement: \begin{align*} & 2\tau^\prime(u) - 2\tau^\prime(u/2) - \frac u2\tau^{\prime\prime}(c) - u\tau^{\prime\prime}(u/2) \\ \tau^{\prime\prime}\geq0 \qquad&\leq 2\tau^\prime(u) - 2\tau^\prime(u/2) - u\tau^{\prime\prime}(u/2) \\ \text{\cref{lmm:ccpoly} \ref{lmm:ccpoly:dtaylor}} \qquad&\leq u \tau^{\prime\prime}(u/2) - u \tau^{\prime\prime}(u/2) \\ \qquad&= 0 \, . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Chain of elementary inequalities using monotonicity, convexity or concavity of tau', tau'' and tau_sqrt'.

nodes.name: Mechanical lemma mech:16
nodes.statement: Let $\tau\in\setccod3$. Let $u\in[0, \infty)$. Then \begin{equation*} u\tau^\prime(u) - 2u\tau^\prime(u/2) \leq 0 \, . \end{equation*}
conclusions: \begin{equation*} u\tau^\prime(u) - 2u\tau^\prime(u/2) \leq 0 \, . \end{equation*}
nodes.label: mech:16

nodes.name: Proof of Mechanical lemma mech:16
nodes.statement: \begin{align*} & u\tau^\prime(u) - 2u\tau^\prime(u/2) \\ \tau^\prime \smallfrown \qquad&\leq 2u\tau^\prime(u/2) - 2u\tau^\prime(u/2) \\ \qquad&= 0 \, . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Chain of elementary inequalities using monotonicity, convexity or concavity of tau', tau'' and tau_sqrt'.

nodes.name: Mechanical lemma mech:17
nodes.statement: Let $\tau\in\setccod3$. Let $b,c\in[0, \infty)$, $s\in[-1,1]$. Assume $b\leq sc$. Then \begin{align*} & \frac{(1-s)c}2\tau^\prime\brOf{\frac{(1+s)c}2 - b} + 2(1-s)(b+c)\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime( c^2 - 2scb + b^2) - 2\tau^\prime\brOf{\frac{(1-s)c}2} + \\&\hphantom{=}\ \ \frac{(1+s)c}2 \tau^\prime\brOf{\frac{(1+s)c}2} - \tau^\prime(c) - b(1-s)\tau^{\prime\prime}\brOf{\frac{(1-s)c}2} \\&\leq \frac{(1-s)c}2\tau^\prime( c-b) + 2(1-s)(b+c)\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime( (c-b)^2) - 2\tau^\prime\brOf{\frac{(1-s)c}2} + \\&\hphantom{=}\ \ -\frac{(1-s)c}2\tau^\prime( c) - b(1-s)\tau^{\prime\prime}\brOf{\frac{c-b}2} \, . \end{align*}
conclusions: \begin{align*} & \frac{(1-s)c}2\tau^\prime\brOf{\frac{(1+s)c}2 - b} + 2(1-s)(b+c)\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime( c^2 - 2scb + b^2) - 2\tau^\prime\brOf{\frac{(1-s)c}2} + \\&\hphantom{=}\ \ \frac{(1+s)c}2 \tau^\prime\brOf{\frac{(1+s)c}2} - \tau^\prime(c) - b(1-s)\tau^{\prime\prime}\brOf{\frac{(1-s)c}2} \\&\leq \frac{(1-s)c}2\tau^\prime( c-b) + 2(1-s)(b+c)\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime( (c-b)^2) - 2\tau^\prime\brOf{\frac{(1-s)c}2} + \\&\hphantom{=}\ \ -\frac{(1-s)c}2\tau^\prime( c) - b(1-s)\tau^{\prime\prime}\brOf{\frac{c-b}2} \, . \end{align*}
nodes.label: mech:17

nodes.name: Proof of Mechanical lemma mech:17
nodes.statement: Apply \begin{align*} \tau^\prime( (s+1)c/2-b) &\leq \tau^\prime( c-b)\, , && s\leq 1,\tau^\prime\nearrow\, ,\\ \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime( c^2 - 2scb + b^2) &\leq \tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime( (c-b)^2)\, ,&& s\leq 1,\tau_{\!\sqrt{}}^\prime\searrow\, ,\\ \tau^\prime( (s+1)c/2) &\leq \tau^\prime(c)\, ,&& s\leq 1,\tau^\prime\nearrow\, ,\\ -\tau^{\prime\prime}((1-s)c/2) &\leq -\tau^{\prime\prime}((c-b)/2)\, ,&& b\leq sc,\tau^{\prime\prime}\searrow \, . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Chain of elementary inequalities using monotonicity, convexity or concavity of tau', tau'' and tau_sqrt'.
